.opencode/skills/vantrilex-workflow-forge/SKILL.md | 263 | 13115 | sha256=25bd20cb38a4289dbc9b87fc49cf2e20bdbe198f89e2afd8f85ec9a63e7b33f2
<!-- BEGIN VERBATIM: .opencode/skills/vantrilex-workflow-forge/SKILL.md -->
---
name: vantrilex-workflow-forge
description: Authors the standing methodology for each task — use when
  a new task starts, before execution begins, so the workflow is fixed
  before the first dispatch.
---

# Vantrilex Workflow-Forge

## Purpose

Vantrilex Workflow-Forge is the WORK-design skill of the Arsenal. It
answers one question — how is this task run? — by authoring the standing
methodology for each task before execution begins, so execution never
invents its own process mid-task. Four top-level skills exist in one
fixed order: `vantrilex-prime` orients the machine, `vantrilex-vanguard`
equips the project, the forge authors the per-task workflow, and
`vantrilex-doctrine` governs the work. The forge runs third in that
order, at every task start, and owns one artifact: the two-part
`WORKFLOW.md` in the target project root, with the standing methodology
in Part A and the current-task workflow in Part B.

Under OpenCode V2 a skill id is its directory path: this skill is
`vantrilex-workflow-forge` because it lives at
`.opencode/skills/vantrilex-workflow-forge/SKILL.md`, and Vanguard proves
the install by reading that path back. The frontmatter `description` is
mandatory because the router reads it when deciding whether to load the
skill; the frontmatter `name` is display-only and must equal the folder
name. The install command and its read-back proof live in the Forge skill
install section of `vantrilex-vanguard`, which is their single home —
this file states neither, and carries no copy of either.

## When to Use

- At the start of every task, before planning or dispatching anything.
- When a new task opens while an old one is still on disk: Part B turns
  over, Part A stays.
- When the methodology drifted mid-task and the standing text no longer
  describes how the work runs.
- When the owner asks how a task will be run, which workflow applies to
  it, or where the current workflow is written down.
- At every equip run and every later run that seeds or repairs the target
  root `WORKFLOW.md` from the canonical copy this skill carries.

## Do NOT use

- To equip a project. State detection, source surveying, kit selection,
  and installation belong to `vantrilex-vanguard`; the forge consumes the
  equipped kit and never selects it.
- To orient a machine or name the system. That is `vantrilex-prime`.
- To rule on laws, gates, roles, or halts. That is `vantrilex-doctrine`;
  the forge authors the workflow the laws govern and never adjudicates
  it.
- To execute the task. The forge writes the workflow, then hands off; a
  forge run that dispatches work has left scope.
- To restate a mechanism another skill owns. The halt block and the
  incident-report template live in `circuit-breaker-guard`; the anchor
  block lives in `session-context-primer`. This file names both homes and
  carries no copy of any of them.
- To seed Part A from memory. The canonical A1-through-A7 text lives
  beside this skill at `assets/workflow-md-template.md`; a Part A written
  from memory invents the very method the run exists to pin down.
- To carry standing method in Part B or per-task choice in Part A. The
  parts never blur; a blur fails the close gate.

## Inputs

- The task description as the owner phrased it, and whether the task is
  new, a modification, or a continuation with a parked lane.
- The live target project files, read before anything is written: the root
  `AGENT.md`, the root `WORKFLOW.md` with its Part A revision notes, and
  the kit region of the root `AGENTS.md` that names which files open every
  task. The doctrine skill owns that region; this file carries no copy of
  its text.
- The canonical Part A text beside this skill at
  `assets/workflow-md-template.md`, read live at seed time.
- The kit in force, read from `kit/kit.lock`: the phase and tier of every
  entry the workflow may load. The lock decides; no printed table in any
  skill file overrules it.
- Owner decisions at the gates the workflow names. No gate is assumed
  approved.

## Procedure

Run F.1 through F.6 in order at every task start. Each step produces a
fact the next step consumes; a step with nothing to consume is reported,
never guessed at.

### F.1 — Read the live files first

Read the root `AGENT.md` and the root `WORKFLOW.md` before planning or
dispatching anything, then the kit region of the root `AGENTS.md`. Record
what each file currently says: the open task, the standing methodology in
force, the dated revision notes on Part A, and the per-task workflow
still on disk from the previous task. When a file is absent, report it
absent; Vanguard seeds missing roots in the docs lane, and the forge
never reconstructs a file it has not read.

### F.2 — Confirm the task and its turnover state

State in one sentence whether the task is new, modified, or a
continuation, and whether Part B turns over. A new task replaces Part B
wholesale. A modification keeps Part B and re-authors the sections the
change touches. A continuation keeps both parts untouched and the forge
run ends after confirming them. Completed work is never re-derived: a
re-plan covers exactly the phases that have not run.

### F.3 — Author the seven sections

Write the per-task workflow in exactly these seven sections, in this
order. Every section carries content; a section with nothing to say
carries `none — because <reason>` with the reason stated, because an
empty section reads as unfinished while an explained absence reads as a
decision.

```text
| # | Section           | Holds                                              |
| 1 | Methodology       | How this task runs: phases, gates, done state      |
| 2 | Roles             | Which role owns each phase and decides each gate   |
| 3 | Precautions       | What must hold before each phase starts            |
| 4 | Repair states     | What a blocked or failed gate does, and the resume |
| 5 | Research          | What must be read or proven before execution       |
| 6 | Expanded thinking | The per-task extras this run needs, and no more    |
| 7 | Kit loadout       | Locked components per phase, read from the lock    |
```

Methodology states phases, gates, and done; it never restates doctrine
law — it names the workflow the laws govern. Roles assigns owners; the
role definitions themselves live in the doctrine skill. Precautions are
preconditions with evidence, not advice. Repair states name the halt,
the resume condition, and the note Part A receives. Research lists
sources with what each must yield. Expanded thinking holds the extras
the task genuinely needs; padding here is scope creep written down. Kit
loadout is read from the lock in force: id plus phase plus tier per
entry, pruned at each phase transition, with the MCP cap as backstop. A
printed mapping never overrules the lock.

### F.4 — Land the two-part artifact

Seed Part A of the target root `WORKFLOW.md` from the canonical copy
beside this skill, read live — never from memory — with items A1 through
A7 kept in order. Write Part B from the seven sections F.3 authored. When
Part A already matches the canonical copy, keep it untouched and say so;
an identical rewrite hides whether the text was verified or merely
rewritten. The artifact spec, with the never-blurred rule, lives under
Outputs; this step executes it.

### F.5 — Announce the plan before the first injection

Print the workflow before anything is injected and let the owner read it.
A plan presented after the kit is already in context cannot be corrected
without spending the injection to get there, so the announce is the last
cheap moment to change the plan. Proceed only on explicit owner sign-off
where the workflow names a gate.

### F.6 — Hand off to execution

Name the next owner of the decision and the trigger that moves it there,
then stop. The forge authors; the orchestrator dispatches under doctrine
governance. A forge run that performs project work, edits beyond the
workflow artifact, or dispatches a subagent has left scope — cut the
section and hand off.

### Revision (§4.4) — dated Part A notes

Part B turns over freely with the work: replace it when the task turns
over and say so in one line. Part A changes only with a dated revision
note appended under its Revision notes heading, stating the date, what
changed, and why — one line per change. A Part A edit without that note
fails the close gate and the run stays open; the note is the proof the
standing method moved deliberately rather than drifted. When the
methodology did not change, no note is written and the close record says
so explicitly. No task closes without its two landings: the Part A note
when the methodology changed, and the per-task `AGENT.md` update the
doctrine rituals require beside it.

## Outputs

- The two-part target root `WORKFLOW.md`, in this shape:

```text
# WORKFLOW.md

<one paragraph: Part A is standing, Part B turns over>

## Part A — Standing methodology

<items A1 through A7, copied from the canonical text the forge
carries, in order>

### Revision notes

<one dated line per change, or the standing no-revisions line>

## Part B — Current-task workflow

<the seven sections F.3 authored for the task in flight>
```

- Part A is standing methodology: task-independent, changed rarely, every
  change dated. Part B is the current-task workflow: task-particular,
  replaced on turnover. The parts never blur: standing method restated in
  Part B is a second copy that will drift — cut it and point at Part A. A
  per-task choice recorded in Part A without a dated note fails the close
  gate — move it to Part B or date the note.
- The announce: the printed workflow from F.5 with the owner sign-off it
  received, so the record shows the plan was read before it ran.
- Nothing else. The forge writes the workflow artifact and the announce;
  it creates no project file, no registry entry, and no documentation.

### Worked example end to end

Task: add request-id logging to the checkout service, owner-approved,
one concern, starting clean.

F.1 reads the live files: `AGENT.md` names the checkout service and its
current release; `WORKFLOW.md` carries Part A matching the canonical
copy with no revision notes; the kit region names the two files that
open every task. F.2 confirms: new task, Part B turns over wholesale.
F.3 authors the seven sections: Methodology names plan, build, and
review with the two-axis review gate and merge as the done state; Roles
assigns the plan to the orchestrator, the build to one Implementer
worktree, the verdict to the Guide; Precautions requires the service
test command recorded green before the build starts; Repair states sends
a failing probe to the bugfix workflow under its own defect id; Research
lists the checkout request path plus the logger docs with what each must
yield; Expanded thinking carries `none — because one concern needs no
auxiliary lanes`; Kit loadout reads the lock live and injects wayfinder
and ask-matt for plan, tdd for build, and code-review for review. F.4
seeds Part A from the canonical copy — already matching, so kept
untouched and reported so — and writes Part B from the seven sections.
F.5 prints the workflow; the owner signs off. F.6 names doctrine
governance as the next owner and stops. The build lands, review passes
on both axes, and the close carries no Part A note — the methodology did
not change — beside the per-task `AGENT.md` update the rituals require.

## Failure Modes

- **Execution starts before the forge run.** The start gate fails and the
  run stops before the first dispatch. A workflow authored after work
  began describes what happened, not what was decided.
- **Part A is seeded from memory.** The docs gate blocks: the canonical
  copy was unreadable or skipped, and seeding from memory invents the
  method the run exists to pin down. Report the block; never guess.
- **A section is empty without its reason.** The workflow is incomplete:
  `none — because <reason>` is a decision, an empty section is a gap.
  Refuse the handoff until every section speaks.
- **The parts blur.** Standing method in Part B is cut to a pointer;
  per-task choice in Part A moves to Part B or earns its dated note. A
  blur found at close fails the gate and the run stays open.
- **A task closes without both landings.** The dated Part A note when the
  methodology changed, plus the per-task `AGENT.md` update beside it. A
  close missing either fails the gate.
- **The run drifts into execution.** Performing project work, editing
  beyond the workflow artifact, or dispatching a subagent is scope
  failure: cut the section and hand off to the orchestrator.
- **A count, hash, or gate verdict is quoted from memory.** Counts come
  from the tree, hashes from the command that printed them, verdicts from
  the script that ran. A remembered number that no longer matches the
  tree is a silent lie.
- **A verification script runs and the session paraphrases it.** Paste the
  output and the exit code as printed. A check that cannot be evaluated
  is a failed check, never a skipped one, and never a pass.

.opencode/skills/vantrilex-workflow-forge/assets/workflow-md-template.md | 68 | 2540 | sha256=20b6644faebee8f3fb9e99efad47122512923e7a7ad61d3e8b433fff24cc82ec
<!-- BEGIN VERBATIM: .opencode/skills/vantrilex-workflow-forge/assets/workflow-md-template.md -->
# WORKFLOW.md

This file carries the standing methodology in Part A and the current-task
workflow in Part B. Part B turns over with the work; Part A changes only
with a dated revision note. The forge skill carries this canonical copy;
Vanguard seeds the target root from it read live, never from memory.

## Part A — Standing methodology

### A1 — Methodology

Every task runs a written workflow fixed before the first dispatch. The
workflow names its phases in order, the gate that closes each phase, and
the done state. Execution never invents process mid-task: a step with no
written workflow waits for one.

### A2 — Roles

One orchestrator authors the workflow and dispatches; subagents execute
exactly one concern each. Only the orchestrator writes `AGENT.md` and
`WORKFLOW.md`. Who decides each gate is named in the workflow before the
phase starts.

### A3 — Precautions

No phase starts until its preconditions are observed and recorded: live
files read, kit in force confirmed, prior gate signed off. A claim
without its observation is not reported; a gate without evidence does
not pass.

### A4 — Repair states

A blocked gate stops the run before the next dispatch; a failed gate
returns the work to its owner with the evidence attached. Every repair
that moves standing method lands a dated note, and the run resumes only
on the condition the note states.

### A5 — Research

Before execution may start, the run reads what the task touches and
proves what it assumes: the live project files, the lock entries it will
inject, and the sources its workflow names. Nothing is reconstructed
from memory.

### A6 — Expanded thinking

Per-task extras live in Part B beside the task they serve, and only
while the task runs. Standing text stays lean: an extra that outlives
its task is either promoted to Part A with its dated note or cut.

### A7 — Kit loadout

Components inject per phase from the lock in force and prune at each
transition; the MCP cap holds as backstop. The lock entry decides what
injects — never an id alone, never a printed table.

### Revision notes

No revisions yet. Append one line per change: the date, what changed,
and why.

## Part B — Current-task workflow

Write the workflow of the task in flight in the seven sections the forge
procedure names: Methodology, Roles, Precautions, Repair states,
Research, Expanded thinking, Kit loadout. Every section carries content
or `none — because <reason>` with the reason stated. Replace this part
when the task turns over; Part A stays.

.opencode/skills/vs-circuit-breaker-guard/SKILL.md | 142 | 7227 | sha256=cdf8799f4146429b71305492b0d496353dbe61afc2f84253a57dcf904d0d7bef
<!-- BEGIN VERBATIM: .opencode/skills/vs-circuit-breaker-guard/SKILL.md -->
---
name: vs-circuit-breaker-guard
description: Use when the same defect has survived three consecutive failed fix attempts — it enforces the 3-strike circuit breaker by tracking strikes per defect id, halting all execution, and emitting a Diagnostic Incident Report instead of a blind fourth attempt.
---

# Circuit Breaker Guard

## Purpose

Protect the project from unbounded debugging loops. This skill implements
constitutional law 2, "3-strike circuit breaker": when the same defect survives 3
consecutive failed fix attempts, all execution halts immediately and the agent emits a
Diagnostic Incident Report (DIR) for human review.

A fix attempt counts as **failed** when the failing test or observed behavior is
unchanged after the attempt. The strike ledger is tracked per defect id, so unrelated
defects never consume each other's budget. The Guide owns this gate: strikes reset only
when the Guide approves a changed hypothesis, or the Leader re-scopes the work. Nothing
else — including user pressure — reopens the loop.

## When to Use

- In the build phase, and in the bugfix workflow, whenever a fix is about to be applied
  to an already-failing test or defect.
- Whenever a defect id has been assigned and a fix attempt is about to be applied.
- Whenever a second or third failed attempt on the same defect id is detected, to arm
  the halt.
- After a Guide-approved changed hypothesis, to reset and rebuild the ledger correctly.

## Do NOT use

- Greenfield work with no failing contract: there is no defect id and nothing to count.
- A shared or global counter: the ledger is always scoped to one root symptom, never to a
  session, a branch, or a file.
- A cosmetic variation of the same defect (new stack trace, shifted line number,
  reworded error) as grounds for a fresh ledger. Only a genuinely different root symptom
  earns a new defect id.

## Inputs

- Defect id (`DEF-<NNN>`), assigned at first detection of the failure.
- The failing test or behavioral probe that proves the defect exists.
- Exactly one hypothesis per fix attempt, plus the evidence collected after running it.
- The strike ledger (session notes keyed by defect id).
- Git history of fix-attempt commits, used to rebuild a lost ledger.

## Procedure

1. **Open a ledger entry.** On first detection, assign the defect id and create its
   ledger entry: `{defect id, root symptom, strikes: 0}`. State the root symptom as an
   invariant description of the wrong behavior, not the stack trace of the moment.
2. **State the hypothesis before touching code.** Every attempt begins with one
   falsifiable hypothesis written into the ledger. No hypothesis, no attempt.
3. **Apply exactly one fix per attempt.** One attempt equals one coherent change
   addressing the stated hypothesis. Do not bundle speculative changes.
4. **Re-run the failing test or probe.** Compare the behavior to the previous attempt.
5. **Score the attempt.**
   - Behavior resolved: close the ledger entry; the defect is fixed.
   - Behavior unchanged: record one strike — append the hypothesis and its evidence
     (test output, diff, measurements) to the ledger for that defect id.
6. **Check the count after every strike.** Strikes 1 and 2: continue the loop at
   step 2. Strike 3: go to step 7 immediately.
7. **HALT.** Print the exact halt message below verbatim, then stop all execution —
   no edits, no tests, no worktree activity, no parallel agents. Never attempt a blind
   fourth fix.
8. **Emit the Diagnostic Incident Report.** Fill the DIR template in Outputs directly
   from the ledger: one hypothesis-log entry per strike, each backed by evidence.
9. **Reset only through the Guide or the Leader.** Present the DIR to the Guide. If the
   Guide approves a changed hypothesis, record the approval, reset the strike count to
   zero, and resume at step 2 with the new hypothesis. The Leader may instead re-scope
   the work, which is recorded in the DIR as a scope change. Without one of those, remain
   halted.

### Exact Halt Message

Print verbatim, substituting the real defect id:

```text
Single home: circuit-breaker-guard — see that skill; not restated here.
All execution stops now. There will be no fourth attempt, blind or otherwise.
Strikes reset only when the Guide approves a changed hypothesis.
Emitting Diagnostic Incident Report for review.
```

## Outputs

- A maintained strike ledger entry for every active defect id.
- On strike 3: the exact halt message above, printed verbatim.
- On strike 3: a completed Diagnostic Incident Report in this exact form:

```text
Single home: circuit-breaker-guard — see that skill; not restated here.
Defect ID:        DEF-<id>
Phase / Worktree: <build phase and worktree where the defect lives>
Symptom:          <root symptom, stated invariantly>

Hypothesis Log (one entry per strike):
  Strike 1:
    Hypothesis:  <what we believed caused the defect>
    Fix Applied: <the change made under this hypothesis>
    Evidence:    <test output / observation proving the behavior did not change>
  Strike 2:
    Hypothesis:  <what we believed caused the defect>
    Fix Applied: <the change made under this hypothesis>
    Evidence:    <test output / observation proving the behavior did not change>
  Strike 3:
    Hypothesis:  <what we believed caused the defect>
    Fix Applied: <the change made under this hypothesis>
    Evidence:    <test output / observation proving the behavior did not change>

Ranked Root Causes (most likely first, justified by the evidence above):
  1. <root cause candidate and the evidence that supports it>
  2. <root cause candidate and the evidence that supports it>
  3. <root cause candidate and the evidence that supports it>

Recommended Unblock Actions:
  1. <action that gathers missing information, e.g. reproduce outside the worktree,
     add tracing, profile the failing path>
  2. <proposed changed hypothesis for the Guide to evaluate>

Guide Sign-off (changed hypothesis approved): ______________________  Date: __________
Strikes reset ONLY on this sign-off.
```

Record the halt itself in `docs/17-CHECKPOINT.md`, and any approved hypothesis change in
`docs/03-architecture/13-ARCHITECTURE-DECISION-RECORD.md`, so the next session inherits
the circuit state instead of rediscovering it.

## Failure Modes

- **Defect mutates slightly between attempts** — new stack trace, shifted line number,
  different error text. Treat it as the same defect and keep counting strikes whenever
  the root symptom is identical; only a genuinely different root symptom earns a new
  defect id and a fresh ledger.
- **User pressure to continue** ("just try once more"). Hold the halt. Offer the DIR as
  the fastest path forward and state that resumption requires a Guide-approved changed
  hypothesis; do not run a fourth attempt under any circumstances.
- **Ledger lost mid-session** (context compaction, crashed shell, fresh terminal).
  Rebuild it from the git history of fix-attempt commits on the defect's branch: each
  attempt commit paired with the test output it produced reconstructs one hypothesis-log
  entry. If any strike cannot be reconstructed with evidence, keep the higher count and
  flag the gap explicitly in the DIR.

<!-- BEGIN VERBATIM: .opencode/skills/vs-github-release-packager/SKILL.md -->
---
name: vs-github-release-packager
description: Use when cutting a release — governs the release lane end to end by requiring the Clean Code, Test and Docs second-pass guards, deriving the semantic version from conventional commits, refusing to publish from a dirty worktree or a missing changelog entry, tagging, publishing with gh release, and verifying from a fresh clone.
---

# GitHub Release Packager

## Purpose

Govern the release path end to end: guard sign-off, changelog entry, semantic version
derivation, annotated tag, publication, and post-release verification. This is the
executable form of the Release workflow, whose order is fixed — three second-pass guards,
then changelog, then semver check, then tag, then publish, then verify.

A release is the one moment where the repository's history becomes immutable, so every
step here is a refusal point first and an action second. The packager declines to publish
on any missing precondition rather than publishing and repairing afterwards.

**Sole release executor — prep-only boundary.** This skill is the SOLE executor of the
release lane: the annotated tag, the push, and the published release happen here and
nowhere else. The `Vantrilex-Releaser` agent stages the prep-only handoff package that
feeds this skill and never publishes; it never duplicates or bypasses this skill.
A dispatch that asks any other agent to tag, push, or publish is refused and escalated,
never obeyed.

## When to Use

- Cutting a version from a guarded, passing codebase.
- Deriving the next semantic version from commit history and checking it against the
  latest tag.
- Publishing a tagged GitHub release and verifying it afterwards.
- Deciding whether a pending set of changes is releasable at all.

## Do NOT use

- To retroactively justify a version already chosen. The version is derived from commit
  history; if the derived version is inconvenient, the commits are wrong, not the rule.
- On a dirty worktree, or with a missing `CHANGELOG.md` entry. Both are refusals, not
  warnings.
- To publish a hotfix straight from a feature branch. Merge through the review phase
  first, so the tag points at reviewed code.
- To rewrite or move an existing published tag. A published `vX.Y.Z` is permanent; a
  correction ships as a new version.

## Inputs

- `CHANGELOG.md`, which must contain an entry for the pending version in the same change.
- Conventional commits since the last `vX.Y.Z` tag.
- The guard results for the three second-pass guards: Clean Code, Test, Docs.
- Authenticated `gh` CLI and a clean git worktree.
- A `RELEASE_NOTES.md` staging file for the composed release notes.

## Procedure

### Part 1 — Guard sign-off

1. Confirm the three second-pass guards passed on the exact commit being released. All
   three must be green before a release is cut:
   - **Clean Code guard** — lint and typecheck clean.
   - **Test guard** — the full test suite passes; no skipped or quarantined test is
     riding along in the release commit.
   - **Docs guard** — every user-visible change has a `CHANGELOG.md` entry and every
     relative link resolves. This guard fails a release without a changelog entry.
2. Refuse to continue if any guard is red or was not run. Name the failing guard and stop.

### Part 2 — Release governance

3. Check the mandatory preconditions and refuse to proceed if either fails:

   ```
   git status --porcelain                     # must print nothing
   grep -n "<pending-version>" CHANGELOG.md   # must match
   ```

4. Derive release notes by merging the `CHANGELOG.md` entry for the pending version with
   the conventional commits since the last tag:

   ```
   git log "$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD" --pretty=format:"- %s"
   ```

5. Run the semver check: a breaking change (`feat!` or a `BREAKING CHANGE` footer)
   requires a MAJOR bump, new features require MINOR, fixes and chores require PATCH.
   Compare the result against the latest `vX.Y.Z` tag and block on any mismatch.
6. Publish using this checklist, in this order — the annotated tag is pushed first, so
   the release can never exist without its tag:

   ```
   gh auth status                                                # must show a logged-in account
   git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "vX.Y.Z" && git push origin vX.Y.Z       # annotated tag, pushed
   gh release create vX.Y.Z --title "vX.Y.Z" --notes-file RELEASE_NOTES.md
   ```

7. Post-release verification: confirm badge URLs resolve against live endpoints; run the
   clone-from-scratch test — fresh clone, install per Quick Start, execute the documented
   command; confirm the release page renders the notes.

## Outputs

- Guard sign-off recorded for Clean Code, Test and Docs against the released commit.
- Drafted release notes derived from `CHANGELOG.md` plus conventional commits.
- Annotated tag `vX.Y.Z` pushed to origin, with a published GitHub release.
- Post-release verification report covering badge URLs, fresh-clone behavior and the
  rendered release page.
- The released version recorded in `docs/17-CHECKPOINT.md`.

## Failure Modes

- **Dirty worktree**: refuse to release; instruct the operator to commit or stash and
  re-run from step 3.
- **Unauthenticated `gh` CLI**: emit the exact remediation command `gh auth login`, then
  re-run `gh auth status` before continuing.
- **Missing changelog entry**: block the release and offer to draft the missing entry from
  the conventional commits since the last tag, subject to Guide approval before proceeding.
- **Semver mismatch**: a breaking change paired with a non-major bump blocks the release;
  require the correct major bump and an updated `CHANGELOG.md` in the same change.
- **A second-pass guard never ran**: treat an unrun guard exactly as a failed guard. A
  release cut without recorded guard evidence is a release cut without proof.
- **Fresh clone fails**: the release is defective regardless of what `gh release` reported.
  Cut a PATCH release with the fix; never amend or move the published tag.

<!-- END VERBATIM: .opencode/skills/vs-github-release-packager/SKILL.md -->

---
name: vs-ponytail
description: Use when a code-executing agent starts a coding task, gates a diff, or surveys repo health, so the ponytail trio routes each job to its variant with the dual guardrail verdict attached.
---

# Vs Ponytail

## Purpose

Polished single-cycle bundle for backlog item `ponytail` (eval record `P1-EVAL-INSTALLED.jsonl` line 11, overall verdict `non-green`). It closes the recorded gaps — D2 no executable pin, D3 no worked example, D7 misrouting description — and makes the D6 live evidence self-sufficient inside the file by embedding the fetched reference table with hashes, bytes, and verbatim quotes.

Single-home pointers (repair1 precedent: markers become pointers, never duplicates):

- Upstream prose lives upstream. The three bodies are adopted, never restated here; see the pinned raw URLs in Procedure step 2.
- Guardrail wiring lives in `.opencode/skills/ponytail/GUARDRAILS.md`; see that file. The FLOOR and CEILING lines below are the verbatim grep anchors that wiring mandates (GUARDRAILS.md lines 41-42), not a second home.
- The eval record lives in `P1-EVAL-INSTALLED.jsonl`; cited by line, never copied in full.

FLOOR: "Be lazy about the solution, never reckless about the change: include tests for risky logic, keep error handling and validation at trust boundaries, and never skip safety for brevity."

CEILING: "Be senior, never astronaut: no gold-plating, no speculative abstraction, no framework-for-one-use, and no option, config, or wrapper nobody asked for."

## When to Use

- A code-executing agent starts a coding task (write, fix, refactor, dependency choice): load core (`ponytail`), default level `full`.
- A diff, branch, or pull request is ready for a gate verdict: load review (`ponytail-review`), report-only.
- A repo-wide health view is needed: load audit (`ponytail-audit`), map-first, at most 20 ranked findings.
- A level choice is needed: pass `lite`, `full` (default), or `ultra` as a runtime argument to core, never as separate entries.
- Safety or leanness is in doubt: enforce FLOOR as the build breaker and CEILING as the leanness breaker through `.opencode/skills/ponytail/GUARDRAILS.md`.

### Should-fire probes

| Probe | Expected route |
|---|---|
| `start this coding task lean` | core, level `full`, dual guardrail on |
| `gate this branch before merge` | review, report-only, Must/Should/Nice findings |
| `survey repo health this quarter` | audit, map-first, at most 20 findings |

## Do NOT use

- For non-coding requests: `summarize this meeting` stays silent, and no variant loads.
- Core for a gating job: `gate this diff` must route review, never core. The v0 description (`any coding task`) misfired exactly here (eval record line 11, false_friends probe); the narrowed frontmatter description above is the fix.
- Review or audit to write code, or core to certify its own output: generation and gating stay in separate invocations.
- The deferred satellites `ponytail-debt`, `ponytail-gain`, or `ponytail-help` through this bundle; they stay out of the minimum set.
- Forked or rewritten upstream body text: adopt the pinned pointer and verify the hash instead.
- Paraphrased guardrails: only the verbatim FLOOR and CEILING lines satisfy the wiring.
- The `.openclaw/skills/...` alias as the pin: note it as an alias, pin the canonical `skills/...` path, verify the hash.

### Near-miss negatives

| Near-miss | Why it stays silent or routes elsewhere |
|---|---|
| `gate this diff` with core loaded | Misroute: a generation posture cannot certify; route review (recorded misfire, fixed by the narrowed description) |
| `summarize this meeting` | Non-coding request: no variant loads |
| `install ponytail on a new machine` | Provisioning job: needs the installer path, not an execution posture |
| `explain what ponytail is` | Reading-about job: quote the pinned pointer, do not load the posture |

### Description-improver note

The v0 description `Use when a code-executing agent starts any coding task, so generation stays lean under the mandatory floor and ceiling guardrails.` fired core on the near-miss `gate this diff`, which needs review (eval record line 11, false_friends outcome `MISFIRE`). The v1 description names the trio routing — `starts a coding task, gates a diff, or surveys repo health` — and re-runs the three should-fire probes plus the four near-misses above with the outcomes stated. The description line responsible is the frontmatter `description`, quoted verbatim in the file head.

## Inputs

- The coding task or the artefact under gate: task text, diff, branch, or pull request reference.
- The selected variant: core, review, or audit, plus the core level (`lite`, `full`, or `ultra`) when core applies.
- The pinned upstream pointer and its verified content hash: the canonical `skills/...` raw URL from the pin table plus the `SHA256=` value the verify command must print.
- The verbatim FLOOR and CEILING lines from Purpose, enforced through `.opencode/skills/ponytail/GUARDRAILS.md`.
- The verification currently passing, so the gate knows what has already been ruled out.

## Procedure

1. **Select the variant.** Coding task means core; single change means review; whole repo means audit. Record the choice and the core level when core applies. A gating prompt never loads core.
2. **Load the pinned upstream text.** Fetch the canonical raw URL for the selected variant and verify the content hash before use with the exact command below. Precondition: egress to `raw.githubusercontent.com`. Expected result: `STATUS=200` and the printed `SHA256=` equals the pinned value in the table. On any mismatch, or when the fetch cannot run, stop: mark the pin `unverified` with the URL and the output beside it, and escalate with the tool, the command, and its output. Read the connected code, not only the diff, when review or audit runs.

Pin table (fetched live 2026-10-17, every row `STATUS=200`):

| Variant | Canonical raw URL | Bytes | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| core | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dietrichgebert/ponytail/main/skills/ponytail/SKILL.md` | 3496 | `9badd22a32e19cb884e46dfa8d3aae82bb81dfa5484105b8b4f0262df823a509` |
| review | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dietrichgebert/ponytail/main/skills/ponytail-review/SKILL.md` | 5143 | `33fe4ebe22a460924e5d4a261e223df22e409cc94ab76182bee9fb91a3ef022e` |
| audit | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dietrichgebert/ponytail/main/skills/ponytail-audit/SKILL.md` | 5417 | `2b3223a02c386d1263e1b08343cb8eb3a53e444cdafb1d79e26c8ec2a8fcad28` |
| license | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dietrichgebert/ponytail/main/LICENSE` | 1071 | `fb1bc6909ac3ef82d5c22106e32ef682b0cff66788fa915fb9b53b15c9d2f3ab` |

Exact verify command (replace `<URL>` with the row URL):

```text
node -e "const u='<URL>';fetch(u).then(async r=>{const b=Buffer.from(await r.arrayBuffer());const h=require('node:crypto').createHash('sha256').update(b).digest('hex');console.log('STATUS='+r.status+' BYTES='+b.length+' SHA256='+h);});"
```

Observed live quotes (byte-verified against the hashes above):

- Core frontmatter carries `license: MIT` and the body opens `You are a lazy senior developer. The best code is the code never written.`
- Core Never-cut keeps `validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, the calibration real hardware needs, anything the user asked for.`
- Core shortcut convention is written `shortcut: <the limit>, <when to upgrade>`.
- Review closes `Lists findings, changes no code.`
- Audit closes `One-shot report, changes no code.`
- License head reads `MIT License`, then `Copyright (c) 2026 DietrichGebert`.

3. **Enforce FLOOR first.** Demand tests for risky logic, error handling that prevents data loss, and validation at trust boundaries. Missing safety fails the guard; brevity never excuses a skip.
4. **Enforce CEILING second.** Refuse gold-plating, speculative abstraction, framework-for-one-use, and any option, setting, or wrapper nobody asked for. Added shape without a second caller fails the guard.
5. **Apply the variant contract.** Core emits the smallest complete change with reuse order codebase helper, then standard library or platform, then installed dependency, then one-liner, then minimum code, and deletion beats addition. Review orders correct, safe, holds under load, tested, fast, lean, and emits numbered Must fix, Should fix, and Nice to have findings with What, Problem, Fix, and If-we-skip-it plus Verdict, Lean, and Not-checked lines. Audit maps first, traces main flows end to end, and ranks at most 20 findings with Lean savings stated as lines plus dependencies.
6. **Keep the report-only boundary.** Review and audit change no code and change nothing; findings carry a concrete failure case each, and a finding without a case is returned.
7. **Record attribution.** Every output names `dietrichgebert/ponytail`, the used variant and level, the pinned URL and hash result, and the MIT notice.

### Worked example

Task: `Extract the loop in scripts/verify-skills.mjs into a helper, no behavior change.`

Good result (core, level `full`): the helper plus unchanged call sites; battery re-run from the repo root, `node scripts/verify-skills.mjs`, prints `VERDICT: PASS`; verdict lines read `FLOOR: pass — risky loop logic re-covered by the battery re-run exit 0.` and `CEILING: pass — helper only, no new option, config, or wrapper.`; attribution names `dietrichgebert/ponytail`, core/full, the pinned core URL, the `SHA256=` match, and the MIT notice.

Weak result, and where it goes wrong: the same helper plus a speculative `--json` flag nobody asked for fails CEILING, and the removed shape is the `--json` flag. Skipping the battery re-run to save time fails FLOOR, and the missing safety is the re-run exit 0. A good application carries both verdict lines; mimicry carries neither.

## Outputs

- The selected variant and level plus the verified pinned pointer.
- For core: the smallest complete change following the reuse order and the Never-cut list.
- For review: a report-only gate verdict with numbered Must fix, Should fix, and Nice to have findings, each with a concrete failure case.
- For audit: a report-only repo-wide view with at most 20 ranked findings and Lean savings.
- The dual-guardrail verdict: FLOOR pass or fail with the missing safety named, CEILING pass or fail with the removed shape named.
- The attribution line: upstream seat, variant, pinned URL, hash result, and MIT notice.

## Failure Modes

- **Unverified pin.** Fetch fails or the hash differs: stop, mark the pin `unverified` with the URL and output, escalate with tool, command, and output.
- **Reckless brevity.** Tests skipped for risky logic or safety cut for brevity; FLOOR fails the change and the missing check is named.
- **Astronaut seniority.** Abstraction, wrapper, option, setting, or framework added without a caller that needs it; CEILING fails the change and the deleted shape is named.
- **Paraphrased guardrails.** Reworded FLOOR or CEILING text that no grep test can confirm; only the verbatim lines count.
- **Forked bodies.** Locally rewritten upstream prose that drifts within one quarter; adopt the pointer and re-pin instead.
- **Alias pinned.** The `.openclaw/skills/...` alias pinned without hash verification; pin canonical and verify.
- **Generation-gate blur.** Review or audit used to write code, or core used to certify its own output; generation and gating stay in separate invocations.
- **Unranked sprawl.** Audit findings beyond 20 or left unranked; rank by damage and cut the tail.

.opencode/skills/vs-preflight-system-doctor/SKILL.md | 152 | 8169 | sha256=1892c4e056697348d87fdc346375475afd1decf460826071bf83341c2b8033d2
<!-- BEGIN VERBATIM: .opencode/skills/vs-preflight-system-doctor/SKILL.md -->
---
name: vs-preflight-system-doctor
description: Use when entering the build phase or before any mutating or long-running work — validates environment, runtimes, configuration and workspace health with a Node-only PASS/FAIL/SKIPPED table, prints remediation commands, and blocks execution on critical failures.
---

# Preflight System Doctor

## Purpose

Make every run reproducible by verifying the machine before acting on it. Nothing in the
build phase starts until the doctor issues a PASS verdict on all critical checks. It
inspects four areas in order — environment, runtimes, configuration, and workspace — and
produces one actionable report. Run it before `session-context-primer` so the primer
operates on verified ground truth.

The runtime policy is Node-only: zero dependencies, ESM, Node 25 in development with 20 as
the floor. There is no second language runtime and no terminal multiplexer in the
toolchain, so this doctor probes for Node and its two versioned companions and nothing
else.

## When to Use

- As step 0 of the build phase, before any implementation work begins.
- Before regenerating derived registry artifacts, since a stale or absent runtime turns a
  clean regeneration into a partial one.
- Before fanning out into parallel git worktrees, where git hygiene and disk capacity
  matter most.
- Before a release, where `gh` authentication is mandatory.
- Whenever an agent is about to run long-lived or mutating operations in a new shell or
  checkout.

## Do NOT use

- As a substitute for `node scripts/verify-registry.mjs` or
  `node scripts/verify-kit.mjs`. Those prove repository data and kit components; the
  doctor proves the machine. A green doctor says nothing about registry integrity.
- As a component verifier. It confirms the tools exist and are new enough; it does not
  prove a component loads or works.
- To authorize a dirty worktree on its own. A dirty tree may be waived only by an
  explicit operator override recorded in the run log, never by the doctor deciding it is
  acceptable.

## Inputs

- Target repository root (defaults to the current working directory).
- `kit/kit.lock`, the pinned kit manifest, when present.
- `registry/catalog.json`, whose per-component `phase` field scopes kit injection.
- Minimum version policy: node >= 20, git >= 2.30, gh >= 2.40.0.
- Optional explicit override for a dirty workspace, supplied by the operator and recorded
  in the run log.

## Procedure

1. **Declare scope.** Record the repo root, the resolved kit lock path, and the run
   timestamp. Later rows cite these values.
2. **Check the environment.** Detect OS and default shell; probe network egress with
   `git ls-remote --exit-code https://github.com/octocat/Hello-World HEAD`. For any
   long-running process started in this session, require that it write to a log file and
   echo that log path to the operator before the doctor continues.
3. **Check the runtimes.** For node, git, and gh: confirm presence and compare the
   reported version against the minimums above. For gh, additionally run `gh auth status`
   as its own check.

   ```sh
   node --version    # >= 20
   git --version     # >= 2.30
   gh --version      # >= 2.40.0
   gh auth status    # authenticated account required
   ```

4. **Check the configuration.** Confirm `kit/kit.lock` exists and that every component it
   pins appears in `registry/catalog.json` with a `phase` field, so injection can be
   scoped per phase rather than kept hot in every session. If the target project declares
   required env vars (references to `process.env` without defaults, or documented required
   vars), confirm `.env.example` exists and holds no real credential values, only
   stand-ins. If the project needs no env vars, mark this check SKIPPED — never FAIL.
   Scan tracked files for real-looking credentials (AWS access-key ids,
   `ghp_`/`sk-`/`xox` token shapes, long high-entropy literals) so no secret is
   about to be leaked.
5. **Check the workspace.** Require `git status --porcelain` to be empty, or accept an
   explicit operator override recorded in the run log. Verify free disk space on the repo
   volume and on any worktree pool volume; require at least 5 GB free on each.

   ```sh
   git ls-remote --exit-code https://github.com/octocat/Hello-World HEAD   # egress probe
   git status --porcelain                                            # empty, or override logged
   ```

6. **Assign severities before reading results.** Each row is CRITICAL or WARN:
   - CRITICAL: node present and version ok; git present and version ok; gh authenticated
     when the run touches GitHub; `kit/kit.lock` in sync with `registry/catalog.json`;
     `.env.example` present and free of real values (when the project needs env vars;
     otherwise SKIPPED); secret scan clean; clean workspace or logged override; disk
     space.
   - WARN: OS/shell identity; long-running-process log path convention; worktree pool
     disk when the run creates no worktrees.
7. **Print the report.** Emit one table with the columns check, status, detail, and
   remediation command, followed by the overall verdict. Statuses are PASS, FAIL, or
   SKIPPED.
8. **Enforce the verdict.** The verdict is PASS only when no CRITICAL row is FAIL.
   FAIL on any critical check blocks execution immediately — print the report and
   stop. SKIPPED rows (for example, network checks while offline) do not fail the run;
   however, a CRITICAL check that lands on SKIPPED requires explicit operator
   confirmation before execution proceeds. A skip is not a pass.

## Outputs

One report block per run, in this shape:

| Check | Status | Detail | Remediation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OS / shell | PASS | Windows 11, PowerShell 7 | n/a |
| Network egress to github.com | SKIPPED | Offline; degraded to cached checks | Restore connectivity |
| node >= 20 | PASS | 20.11.0 | n/a |
| git >= 2.30 | PASS | 2.45.0 | n/a |
| gh >= 2.40.0 | PASS | 2.57.0 | n/a |
| gh auth status | FAIL | Not authenticated | `gh auth login` |
| kit/kit.lock in sync with registry/catalog.json | FAIL | 2 pinned components carry no `phase` | Set `phase` in the catalog, then regenerate |
| .env.example present, no real values (only when env vars needed) | SKIPPED | Project declares no required env vars | n/a |
| Secret scan of tracked files | PASS | No credential-shaped strings found | n/a |
| Clean git status (or logged override) | FAIL | 3 modified files | Commit, stash, or log an explicit override |
| Long-running process log path echoed | SKIPPED | No long-running process started | n/a |
| Disk space (repo + worktree pool) | PASS | 84 GB and 120 GB free | n/a |

Verdict lines:

```text
PREFLIGHT VERDICT: FAIL — 3 critical check(s) failed. Execution blocked.
PREFLIGHT VERDICT: PASS — all critical checks green. Execution may proceed.
```

Remediation commands are copy-pasteable and reference repository scripts where they
exist: `node scripts/verify-registry.mjs` proves the registry data,
`node scripts/generate-catalog-json.mjs` rebuilds the machine mirror, and
`node scripts/verify-kit.mjs` proves each kit component loads.

## Failure Modes

- **gh not authenticated.** Print the exact login command — `gh auth login` — in the
  remediation column and in the verdict summary, and note that the device-flow login is
  interactive, so the operator must run it personally.
- **Kit lock drift.** A component pinned in `kit/kit.lock` is missing from
  `registry/catalog.json`, or carries no `phase`. List the offending ids explicitly and
  regenerate the mirror with `node scripts/generate-catalog-json.mjs`; do not hand-edit
  the generated JSON.
- **Offline machine.** Degrade gracefully: reuse cached catalog metadata and last-known
  versions, mark every network-dependent check SKIPPED rather than FAIL, and state plainly
  which follow-on steps (cloning, syncing, releasing) cannot run until connectivity
  returns.
- **Node below the floor.** An older runtime will fail the ESM and `node:` built-in
  assumptions this repository is written against. Report the observed version and stop;
  do not attempt the run and explain the failure afterwards.

<!-- END VERBATIM: .opencode/skills/vs-preflight-system-doctor/SKILL.md -->

<!-- BEGIN VERBATIM: .opencode/skills/vs-session-context-primer/SKILL.md -->
---
name: vs-session-context-primer
description: Use when a session starts or context is lost to compaction — rebuilds the working context in about ten seconds from the AI constitution, project summary, git state and circuit-breaker ledger, and emits a single anchor block (single home: session-context-primer).
---

# Session Context Primer

## Purpose

Operationalize "prime context before action" at session start. Within a strict ~10-second
budget it loads the minimum state every role needs (mission, lifecycle phase, worktree
pool, next item, guard status) and emits a single anchor block (single home: session-context-primer) that anchors the
rest of the session. The primer is strictly read-only: it observes, it never edits, never
commits, and never resolves a dirty tree on its own.

## When to Use

- As the first action of any session in a project scaffolded by this kit.
- Immediately after a context reset, conversation compaction, or a cleared session.
- Before resuming work in an existing git worktree.
- Before the docs phase and the build phase, to confirm which phase is actually live.

## Do NOT use

- To repair what it observes. A dirty tree, a broken guard, or an open Diagnostic
  Incident Report is surfaced in the anchor and escalated, not silently fixed here.
- As a substitute for `preflight-system-doctor`. The primer assumes the machine was
  already verified; it does not re-check runtimes or authentication.
- To load project knowledge. If the mission or the next item is genuinely needed in
  depth, read `docs/00-PROJECT-SUMMARY.md` properly instead of stretching this.

## Inputs

- The project root, expected to contain `AGENTS.md` and the numbered docs set under
  `docs/`.
- Read access to git metadata (status, branch, recent commits).
- The circuit-breaker ledger state, if the `circuit-breaker-guard` skill has one open.

## Procedure

Read in strict order. The timebox rule in step 6 overrides everything else.

1. **Read the invariants.** Load `docs/25-AI-CONSTITUTION.md` (immutable laws) and the
   hard rules from `AGENTS.md`. Load these two, not the whole repository guide set.

2. **Read the mission and the checkpoint.** Take the one-liner mission from
   `docs/00-PROJECT-SUMMARY.md`, the current phase and pending item from
   `docs/17-CHECKPOINT.md`, and the guard state from `docs/18-WORKFLOW.md`. Do not open
   `docs/99-archive/`; superseded documents never carry live state.

3. **Read git state.** Current branch, short status, and the last five commits:

   ```bash
   git status --short --branch
   git log --oneline -5
   ```

4. **Read circuit-breaker state, if any.** If the `circuit-breaker-guard` skill has
   recorded strikes or emitted a Diagnostic Incident Report, load its current state: strike
   count, defect id, and the hypothesis the Guide approved. Otherwise record zero strikes.

5. **Emit the anchor (single home: session-context-primer).** Output exactly one fenced block and nothing else:

   ```text
   Single home: session-context-primer — see that skill; not restated here.
   ----------------------------------------------------------
   Mission  : <one-liner from docs/00-PROJECT-SUMMARY.md>
   Phase    : <current lifecycle phase: docs | plan | build | review | operate>
   Branch   : <branch> (<clean|N files changed>)
   Worktrees: <active worktrees, or "none">
   Next     : <top roadmap item id and title from docs/23-ROADMAP.md>
   Guards   : Clean Code <pending|passed> | Test <pending|passed> | Docs <pending|passed>
   Circuit  : <n> strike(s) <or "DIR open">
   ----------------------------------------------------------
   ```

   A filled anchor looks like this:

   ```text
   Single home: session-context-primer — see that skill; not restated here.
   ----------------------------------------------------------
   Mission  : Ship a curated agent component kit onto target projects
   Phase    : build
   Branch   : wt/mech-skills (clean)
   Worktrees: wt-mech-skills (active)
   Next     : R-014 Regenerate catalog mirror and confirm the entry count
   Guards   : Clean Code pending | Test pending | Docs pending
   Circuit  : 0 strikes
   ----------------------------------------------------------
   ```

6. **Respect the hard rule.** If priming exceeds roughly 10 seconds worth of reads (very
   large files, slow storage, many worktrees), stop reading immediately and emit the
   anchor from whatever is loaded, marking unloaded slots as `unknown`. An approximate
   anchor now beats a perfect anchor late.

## Outputs

- Exactly one anchor block (single home: session-context-primer) in the session transcript (about nine lines).
- Nothing written to disk, no commits, no branches created or removed; the primer is
  strictly read-only.

## Failure Modes

- Missing docs: anchor from git state alone (branch, recent commits, dirty files) and
  flag the gap explicitly, for example `Docs unavailable - anchored from git state`.
- Oversized constitution or project summary: read only the invariants and mission
  sections, located by heading, instead of streaming whole files into context.
- Timebox exceeded: stop mid-sequence, emit the partial anchor, and mark unread slots
  `unknown` rather than finishing the read sequence.
- No git repository: anchor from `AGENTS.md` and `docs/25-AI-CONSTITUTION.md` only, and
  flag the missing VCS state.
- Dirty tree or detached HEAD: surface the condition verbatim in the anchor instead of
  resolving it silently; resolution belongs to the Leader.

<!-- END VERBATIM: .opencode/skills/vs-session-context-primer/SKILL.md -->

---
name: vs-smithery
description: Use when a Smithery MCP or skill candidate needs searching, vetting, and single-item admission without bulk installs.
---

# Vs-Smithery

## Purpose

Teach the Smithery search-vet-add loop for one candidate at a time, with vetting before any add and with single-item proposals only. This skill proposes; it never admits in bulk, never writes the lock or the registry, and never executes installs on its own authority. All command facts below are grounded in the R2 bundle smithery section read live via `git show wt/vta-factory-08:VTA-FACTORY-08-R2-method.md` section 4, read-only. Anything beyond that bundle is marked `unverified` and never invented.

## When to Use

- When a Smithery MCP candidate needs searching by keyword before any vetting starts.
- When a Smithery skill candidate needs searching by task phrase before any vetting starts.
- When a found candidate needs a SCAN-FIRST vet verdict plus a provenance check before any proposal.
- When a vetted candidate needs a single-item lock-record proposal with no bulk step.
- When an operator asks how the Smithery CLI loop works and needs the verified command shapes only.

## Do NOT use

- To admit two or more candidates at once. Bulk admission is refused; one candidate yields at most one proposal.
- To invent an install command. A command is either quoted from the R2 bundle section 4.1 or marked `unverified` with a null install and a stated reason.
- To use the `npx @smithery/cli` spelling. The R2 bundle section 4.2 reports it as `unverified` against the registry-verified package name; never treat it as verified.
- To write `kit/kit.lock`, `registry/data/*.jsonl`, `registry/catalog.json`, or any generated catalog Markdown. Those surfaces belong to their single writers.
- To skip SCAN-FIRST vetting. Search results never advance to a proposal without a recorded vet verdict for the same candidate identifier.
- To execute installs from the teaching seat. Teaching and logging only; the downstream single writer owns the write.

## Inputs

- One candidate identifier at a time, either an MCP search term or a skill search term.
- The target client name for an MCP add, or the target agent name for a skill add, stated before the add step is drafted.
- The R2 bundle smithery section, read-only, as the sole command ground truth: package `smithery` version `1.2.0` verified via `https://registry.npmjs.org/smithery/latest`, install `npm install -g smithery@latest` requiring Node.js 20 plus, docs page `https://smithery.ai/docs/concepts/cli`, homepage `https://smithery.ai/`, source repository `https://github.com/smithery-ai/cli`.
- The SCAN-FIRST procedure at `P2-SCAN-FIRST.md`, read live before any vet verdict is recorded.
- The proposal reference files `P3-MCP-A.json` and `P3-MCP-B.json`, used by reference only when a starter example is needed.
- The auth state for the seat: whether `smithery auth login` has completed and what `smithery auth whoami` reports.

## Procedure

Run search, then vet, then add, in that fixed order. Never reorder and never skip vet.

### Search with the verified CLI shapes

1. Confirm the CLI surface from the R2 bundle only. Endorsed install form is `npm install -g smithery@latest` with Node.js 20 plus, and the endorsed invocation shape is `npx smithery` as observed on `https://smithery.ai/`. Every other install spelling is out of scope.
2. Authenticate only through the documented gate: `smithery auth login` followed by `smithery auth whoami`. The bundle Important Notes state authentication is required for some operations.
3. Search MCP candidates with `smithery mcp search "github"` as the shape, replacing the quoted term with the single candidate term. Search skill candidates with `smithery skill search "code review"` as the shape, replacing the quoted phrase with the single task phrase.
4. Scripting note on machine-readable output. The `--json` flag is `unverified` in the R2 bundle: section 4.1 lists no `--json` flag on any command. Prefer machine-readable output only after the live `smithery --help` text on the seat proves the flag exists; until then record the flag as `unverified`, keep human-readable output as the evidence, and never invent flag behavior.
5. Record one search-evidence row per candidate: the exact command run, the seat output quoted, and the registry reference the output names. A candidate with no quoted search evidence does not advance.

### Vet with SCAN-FIRST plus provenance

1. Run SCAN-FIRST first for the same candidate identifier, following `P2-SCAN-FIRST.md` gate order: examine, then scan with the verdict recorded, then classify and route only when clean. A scan hit routes to quarantine; clean items from a hit batch wait held-pending and never advance on momentum.
2. Check provenance second: resolve the registry record at `https://registry.npmjs.org/smithery/latest` for the CLI itself, the docs page `https://smithery.ai/docs/concepts/cli` for the command shape, and the source repository `https://github.com/smithery-ai/cli` for ownership. For the candidate, record the observed count behavior as observed-fluctuate and never exact-today, matching the `P3-MCP-A.json` and `P3-MCP-B.json` observation discipline.
3. Inspect the candidate surface with the vetted read shapes only: `smithery tool list`, `smithery tool find`, and `smithery tool get <connection> <tool>`. Quote the exact output used for the verdict. Shapes beyond these three are `unverified` until the docs page proves them.
4. Record one vet verdict per candidate: `CLEAN` with quoted evidence, or `HIT` with the quarantine reference, or `HOLD` with the reason stated. A proposal needs a recorded `CLEAN` vet verdict; `HIT` and `HOLD` never advance.

### Add as a single-item proposal only

1. Draft at most one lock-record proposal per vetted candidate. The proposal carries tier `conditional`, evaluator `auto-evaluator`, install null with `verification: unverified` unless the install string was verified against a real registry from the seat, and the vet verdict reference.
2. Use the documented add shapes only: `smithery mcp add <url> --client <name>` for MCP candidates and `smithery skill add <skill> --agent <name>` for skill candidates. The bundle Important Notes state the client must restart after adding or removing servers; record the restart as pending until the owner confirms it.
3. Count bulk admissions on every run and keep the count at zero. One run proposes one item; a second candidate starts a new search-vet-add pass with its own evidence. If a bulk step is requested, refuse it, quote the request, and escalate.
4. Leave the write to the downstream single writer. This skill creates the proposal text; it never edits the lock, the registry sidecars, the generated mirror, or any installed tree, and it executes no install.

## Outputs

- One search-evidence row per candidate with the exact command and the quoted output reference.
- One vet verdict per candidate with `CLEAN`, `HIT`, or `HOLD` stated and the SCAN-FIRST plus provenance evidence quoted.
- At most one single-item lock-record proposal per `CLEAN` candidate, carrying `conditional` tier, `auto-evaluator` evaluator, null install with `verification: unverified` unless verified, and the vet reference.
- A bulk count of zero quoted on every run, with the per-item admit-or-hold decision stated per candidate.

## Failure Modes

- **Platform refusal.** Stop and report the exact platform error verbatim with the closest equivalent flagged. Never invent a workaround and never treat the refusal as a pass.
- **Scan hit before classify.** Route to quarantine per `P2-SCAN-FIRST.md`, hold clean companions pending, stage nothing from the hit batch, and escalate with the batch identifier and the finding quoted.
- **Unverified command requested.** Refuse the `npx @smithery/cli` spelling and any shape beyond section 4.1, record the spelling as `unverified`, and propose only through the verified shapes.
- **Bulk admission requested.** Refuse the bulk step, quote the request, keep the bulk count at zero, and continue one candidate at a time or stop for owner direction.
- **Auth gate closed.** Record that `smithery auth login` is pending, run only the operations the bundle marks as unauthenticated, and never record a vet verdict that needed an authenticated read.
- **Restart pending.** Record the required client restart as pending after any add-shape proposal and keep the candidate at proposal state until the owner confirms the reload.
- **Evidence missing.** A search without quoted output, a vet without a recorded verdict, or a proposal without its vet reference is discarded and rerun in gate order.

<!-- END VERBATIM: .opencode/skills/vs-smithery/SKILL.md -->
