/**
 * Vantrilex Guards — V2-only guard carrier for OpenCode.
 *
 * This module registers exactly the documented V2 hook names listed below and
 * nothing else. Every hook it uses cites its docs section in the census; any
 * hook without a citation never ships here.
 *
 * Relationship to Stream G (`../plugin/arsenal.ts`): that module already
 * carries guards proven by a 45/45 probe battery. This module does not
 * reimplement them. It imports and wraps the proven V2 `setup`, so both files
 * arm the same guards with the same verdict text. One-line reason per guard:
 *
 *   - task dispatcher on session "prompt": proven per-turn instruction append
 *     that is idempotent within a turn and offset-safe by appending.
 *   - long-running-process guard plus docs-discipline guard on tool
 *     "execute.before": proven block/warn pair, including shell-text write
 *     recovery for the bash tool.
 *   - typescript-check plus prettier-format on tool "execute.after":
 *     proven conditional toolchain guards that append verdicts and never throw.
 *   - long-running-process guard plus docs-discipline guard on shell
 *     "create.before": proven coverage for raw shell executions, recorded
 *     under anonymous because the event carries no session id.
 *   - plan-guard detective append on session "prompt" (this carrier only):
 *     validates the dispatch brief against the attached plan excerpt and
 *     appends a dated plan-drift report. Observation-only: the turn always
 *     proceeds, so no admission claim is made here (see the fallback note).
 *
 * Hook census (all sections on https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/):
 *
 *   KEPT (registered by the wrapped setup, plus the plan-guard prompt hook
 *   registered by this carrier below):
 *   - session "prompt" — docs section Sessions, Prompt admission.
 *   - session "prompt" (plan-guard detective append) — same docs section
 *     Sessions, Prompt admission. Rewrite-only: appends the drift report and
 *     always lets the turn proceed.
 *   - tool "execute.before" — docs section Hooks, Tools (ToolHooks interface).
 *   - tool "execute.after" — docs section Hooks, Tools (ToolHooks interface).
 *   - shell "create.before" — docs section Hooks, Shell (ShellHookContext).
 *
 *   DROPPED (documented, but no Tier-0 guard lands there):
 *   - session "context" and "compaction" — docs section Sessions, Model
 *     requests. Stuffing guard verdicts into every model call would tax each
 *     request for no per-call decision; admission-time dispatch plus tool
 *     verdicts already cover the Tier-0 set.
 *   - session "generate", "title", "model.request", "http.request",
 *     "http.response", experimental websocket hooks, "retry" — same page.
 *     Enumerated so the omission is deliberate, not an oversight.
 *   - ctx.permission.hook("evaluate", ...) — documented in Permissions and
 *     the migrate-v1 mapping table, but forbidden by the owner allow-all
 *     policy. This module never touches ctx.permission, in code or by
 *     delegation: the wrapped setup registers no permission hook either.
 *   - ctx.storage — documented in Storage. Dropped with intent: the guards
 *     are stateless across runs by design, so no durable key is needed.
 *   - The V1 server() surface — migrate-v1 documents the dual-surface shape,
 *     but this module is V2-only on purpose. V1 stays served by arsenal.ts
 *     on its own path; this file carries no V1 hook name.
 *
 * Shape notes:
 *
 *   - The runtime-visible shape matches the documented contract exactly: a
 *     default export carrying `id` plus `setup`. The `Plugin.define` helper
 *     is the Stream-G-proven structural mirror, imported rather than
 *     redeclared, because the `@opencode/plugin` package is injected by the
 *     OpenCode runtime and is absent from this dependency-free checkout
 *     (only the V1 peer is vendored). A literal bare import would fail the
 *     load smoke and the type check in this repo while behaving identically
 *     under the host.
 *   - The relative specifier keeps its `.ts` extension on purpose. Node
 *     type-stripping resolves the sibling only in that form, while tsc under
 *     nodenext accepts it with allowImportingTsExtensions. This file sits
 *     outside the repo tsconfig `files` list, so the repo gate does not
 *     cover it; the equivalent strict check is run with that flag stated.
 *   - Plugin id is stable and distinct from the Stream-G id so status output
 *     and storage scoping identify this carrier on their own.
 *
 * Coexistence note: V2 discovers local plugins from both `.opencode/plugin/`
 * and `.opencode/plugins/`, so a host that loads arsenal.ts and this carrier
 * registers the same five hooks twice, in plugin order. Expected effects are
 * benign: the dispatcher append is idempotent so the second prompt hook sees
 * the instruction already present and skips; a blocking before-guard throws
 * in the first hook so the second never runs for violations; warn-mode lines
 * may appear twice on one tool result and the serialised type check may run
 * twice per edit. No dedupe logic lives here: silencing a sibling instance
 * from inside setup would be behaviour nobody can see, and the duplication
 * degrades to noise, never to a false PASS.
 *
 * Scope and status of that note, which must be read as one claim with the
 * paragraph above. Two paths, two statuses:
 *
 *   - Dispatcher path — PROVEN, and the only proven part. The append check
 *     reads the draft itself, which both plugins share, so the second prompt
 *     hook sees the instruction already present and skips.
 *   - Warn-flush path — NOT COVERED. Each plugin builds its own
 *     ArsenalContext, so each owns a separate pendingWarnings array, and a
 *     warn-mode docs-discipline or long-running verdict flushed in
 *     `v2ToolAfter` could append the same WARN line twice. Concrete case: one
 *     warn-mode write, two identical WARN lines on one tool result. The
 *     serialised type check running twice per edit sits in the same gap.
 *
 * Status: UNVERIFIED HYPOTHESIS. No two-plugin dual-load runtime proof exists,
 * and the duplicate WARN line has never been reproduced on a host that loads
 * both plugins; nothing above is an observation. Any dedup is deferred to a
 * runtime-proof lane: adding it now would change behaviour nobody can see, on
 * evidence nobody has, and cross-instance state would be equally invisible.
 */

import arsenalPlugin, {
  definePlugin,
  type PluginContextLike,
  type PluginDefinition,
  type SessionPromptEvent,
} from "../plugin/arsenal.ts";

/**
 * V2 `setup`. Delegates to the proven Stream-G setup first (five hooks, no
 * adaptation, no permission access), then registers the plan-guard detective
 * append on session "prompt" (same docs section Sessions, Prompt admission).
 * The five registrations named in the census above are the complete set this
 * registration can produce, and every callback degrades to a no-op for the
 * cases its own comments name.
 *
 * Plan-guard fallback (detective-only, non-blocking): per P1-R0.md verdict (1)
 * the session prompt hook exposes no typed rejection API for prompt admission,
 * so this extension only observes the brief against the attached plan excerpt
 * and appends a dated plan-drift report; the turn always proceeds. Enforcement
 * stays with leader-discipline plus the Verifier gates, not with this hook.
 */
const setup: PluginDefinition["setup"] = async (ctx: PluginContextLike): Promise<void> => {
  await arsenalPlugin.setup(ctx);
  const sessionRegister = ctx?.session?.hook;
  if (typeof sessionRegister !== "function") return;
  await sessionRegister.call(ctx.session, "prompt", (event: SessionPromptEvent): void => {
    try {
      const draft = event?.prompt;
      const text = typeof draft?.text === "string" ? draft.text : "";
      if (text.length === 0) return;
      const annotated = appendPlanDriftReport(text);
      if (annotated === text) return;
      draft.text = annotated;
    } catch {
      return;
    }
  });
};

/* ===========================================================================
 * Plan-guard fallback: detective plan-drift append (non-blocking).
 *
 * Binding: P1-R0.md verdict (1) rules the hard admission gate IMPOSSIBLE on
 * the current host, so nothing here claims to refuse a brief. The functions
 * below compare the dispatch brief against the plan excerpt attached to the
 * same prompt and append a dated plan-drift report when brief identifiers
 * have no match in the plan. Findings are observations for the leader, never
 * verdicts, and the turn always proceeds.
 *
 * Prompt convention (attached by leader-discipline, read by `extractPlanDoc`):
 *
 *   Plan-Doc-Begin: <plan label, e.g. MISSION-PLAN.md>
 *   <actual plan doc lines, 1-based for citations>
 *   Plan-Doc-End
 *   <dispatch brief lines>
 *
 * A prompt without both markers is left untouched. A prompt that already
 * carries a report is left untouched, so the append stays idempotent within
 * a turn. An empty brief, an empty plan excerpt, and a brief whose tokens all
 * match are likewise left untouched.
 *
 * Minimal fixture (illustrative only — not a real plan doc; no AETHER
 * MISSION-PLAN sample exists in this checkout):
 *
 *   Plan-Doc-Begin: MISSION-PLAN.md
 *   Lane VTA-EXPANSION-05 phase P1 opens with node p1-r0.
 *   Node p1-planguard carries the detective plan-guard fallback.
 *   Plan-Doc-End
 *   Brief: lane VTA-EXPANSION-05 P1 node p1-planguard plus extra p9-nowhere.
 *
 * Expected: one finding for `p9-nowhere` on brief line 1, cited against
 * MISSION-PLAN.md lines 1-2, under a header carrying the UTC date.
 * ===========================================================================
 */

/** Tag heading every emitted report; also the idempotency marker. */
export const PLAN_DRIFT_TAG = "[plan-guard] plan-drift report";

/** Opening plan-attachment marker; the label follows the colon. */
export const PLAN_DOC_BEGIN = "Plan-Doc-Begin:";

/** Closing plan-attachment marker; the line must carry nothing else. */
export const PLAN_DOC_END = "Plan-Doc-End";

/**
 * The honestly-documented fallback: states the missing typed-rejection
 * surface and that enforcement is leader-discipline plus Verifier gates.
 */
export const PLAN_GUARD_FALLBACK =
  "Plan-guard fallback (detective-only, non-blocking): per P1-R0.md verdict (1) " +
  "the session prompt hook exposes no typed rejection API for prompt admission, " +
  "so this extension only observes the brief against the attached plan excerpt " +
  "and appends a dated plan-drift report; the turn always proceeds. Enforcement " +
  "stays with leader-discipline plus the Verifier gates, not with this hook.";

/** A plan excerpt with its real label, so citations point at file:line. */
export type PlanDoc = {
  readonly label: string;
  readonly lines: readonly string[];
};

/** One brief identifier with no match anywhere in the attached plan. */
export type PlanDriftFinding = {
  readonly briefLine: number;
  readonly briefToken: string;
  readonly planLabel: string;
  readonly planLinesChecked: number;
};

/** Identifier-shaped tokens: dash- or slash-joined runs carrying a digit. */
const IDENTIFIER_PATTERN = /[A-Za-z0-9]+(?:[-/][A-Za-z0-9]+)+/g;

/** Pure digit-and-dash runs (UTC dates, numeric ranges) are never findings. */
const DATE_LIKE_PATTERN = /^\d+(?:-\d+)+$/;

/**
 * Collects the distinct identifier tokens of a brief, in first-seen order.
 * Tokens without a digit are ordinary hyphenated words and are skipped, as
 * are date-like runs; both would otherwise read as drift on every brief.
 */
export const extractBriefTokens = (briefText: string): string[] => {
  if (typeof briefText !== "string" || briefText.length === 0) return [];
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  const ordered: string[] = [];
  for (const match of briefText.matchAll(IDENTIFIER_PATTERN)) {
    const token = match[0];
    if (!/\d/.test(token)) continue;
    if (DATE_LIKE_PATTERN.test(token)) continue;
    const key = token.toLowerCase();
    if (seen.has(key)) continue;
    seen.add(key);
    ordered.push(token);
  }
  return ordered;
};

/**
 * Splits a prompt into its brief and its attached plan excerpt. Returns a
 * null plan when either marker is absent, so the caller stays silent then.
 */
export const splitBriefAndPlan = (promptText: string): { briefText: string; plan: PlanDoc | null } => {
  if (typeof promptText !== "string" || promptText.length === 0) return { briefText: "", plan: null };
  const lines = promptText.split("\n");
  const beginIndex = lines.findIndex((line) => line.trimStart().startsWith(PLAN_DOC_BEGIN));
  if (beginIndex < 0) return { briefText: promptText, plan: null };
  const endIndex = lines.findIndex((line, index) => index > beginIndex && line.trim() === PLAN_DOC_END);
  if (endIndex < 0) return { briefText: promptText, plan: null };
  const rawLabel = lines[beginIndex].slice(PLAN_DOC_BEGIN.length).trim();
  const label = rawLabel.length > 0 ? rawLabel : "plan-doc";
  const plan: PlanDoc = { label, lines: lines.slice(beginIndex + 1, endIndex) };
  const briefText = [...lines.slice(0, beginIndex), ...lines.slice(endIndex + 1)].join("\n");
  return { briefText, plan };
};

/**
 * Reports every brief token with no case-insensitive match in the plan,
 * citing the brief line of first sighting and the plan line range checked.
 * An empty plan excerpt yields no findings: drift cannot be judged without it.
 */
export const detectPlanDrift = (briefText: string, plan: PlanDoc): PlanDriftFinding[] => {
  const findings: PlanDriftFinding[] = [];
  if (plan === null || plan === undefined) return findings;
  if (plan.lines.length === 0) return findings;
  const haystack = plan.lines.join("\n").toLowerCase();
  const briefLines = briefText.split("\n");
  for (const token of extractBriefTokens(briefText)) {
    const lowered = token.toLowerCase();
    if (haystack.includes(lowered)) continue;
    let briefLine = 0;
    for (let index = 0; index < briefLines.length; index += 1) {
      if (briefLines[index].toLowerCase().includes(lowered)) {
        briefLine = index + 1;
        break;
      }
    }
    findings.push({ briefLine, briefToken: token, planLabel: plan.label, planLinesChecked: plan.lines.length });
  }
  return findings;
};

/**
 * Formats the dated plan-drift report. Each finding cites its brief line and
 * the plan file:line range checked, and the fallback paragraph closes the
 * report so the non-blocking nature travels with every emission.
 */
export const formatPlanDriftReport = (
  plan: PlanDoc,
  findings: readonly PlanDriftFinding[],
  todayUtc: string,
): string => {
  const cited = findings
    .map((finding) => `- \`${finding.briefToken}\` (brief line ${finding.briefLine}) — no match in ${finding.planLabel}:1-${finding.planLinesChecked}`)
    .join("\n");
  return (
    `${PLAN_DRIFT_TAG} — ${todayUtc} (detective, non-blocking)\n` +
    `Plan checked: ${plan.label} (${plan.lines.length} lines)\n` +
    `Brief tokens with no plan match:\n` +
    `${cited}\n` +
    PLAN_GUARD_FALLBACK
  );
};

/**
 * Appends the drift report to a prompt when the brief drifts from the
 * attached plan, and returns the prompt unchanged otherwise. Append-only:
 * the input text is never shortened and admission is never touched.
 */
export const appendPlanDriftReport = (promptText: string, todayUtc?: string): string => {
  if (typeof promptText !== "string" || promptText.length === 0) return promptText;
  if (promptText.includes(PLAN_DRIFT_TAG)) return promptText;
  const { briefText, plan } = splitBriefAndPlan(promptText);
  if (plan === null) return promptText;
  const findings = detectPlanDrift(briefText, plan);
  if (findings.length === 0) return promptText;
  const today = typeof todayUtc === "string" && todayUtc.length > 0 ? todayUtc : new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);
  return `${promptText}\n\n${formatPlanDriftReport(plan, findings, today)}`;
};

export default definePlugin({
  id: "vantrilex-guards",
  setup,
});

<!-- END VERBATIM: .opencode/plugins/vantrilex-guards.ts -->

#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * relay-poll.mjs — relay queue poll hook (vanbu side).
 *
 * Binding: DESIGN.md sections 2-4, POLL.md consumer query (vanbu side),
 * RELAY-SCHEMA.md live shape. Cadence 180 seconds, 300 seconds in quiet
 * mode. One bounded REST queue query per tick, then compare against the
 * watermark. A worker wakes ONLY on new activity; a silent tick costs
 * nothing beyond the single query (COST GUARD, enforced at script level).
 *
 * REST polling: a single data-source query (POST
 * /databases/{database_id}/query) with a server-side filter
 * (to = QUERY_CONSUMER AND status = pending), sorted by created
 * ascending. There is no alternate query path anywhere in this file; the
 * network layer is plain HTTPS against the Notion REST API only.
 * The poll target (QUERY_CONSUMER) is pinned per the POLL.md consumer
 * query; to change the target, change POLL.md first and this constant
 * with it — never drift one without the other.
 * Minimal columns on poll: the tick reads only the routing envelope
 * (id, from, to, type, status, created, last_edited_time, thread_id,
 * retry_count). The full page body is fetched only on wake, one fetch
 * per woken row, never on a silent tick.
 *
 * Quota-aware backoff: HTTP 429 (and 529, treated exactly as 429, plus
 * any usage-limit signal in the response body) retries on an exponential
 * ladder of 30s, then 2m, then 10m, each step with up to 25 percent
 * jitter. A Retry-After response header is always honored and wins over
 * the ladder when it names a longer wait. When the ladder is exhausted
 * the tick degrades: the recommended cadence steps down 180s to 600s to
 * 1800s and the failure is logged loudly instead of retried further,
 * so a quota event can never become a retry storm.
 *
 * Idempotency: created row ids have the form RL-<epoch>-<hex> (epoch
 * seconds plus random lowercase hex), unique per writer without
 * coordination. The claim write is a guarded pending-to-acked transition:
 * the poller re-reads the row and writes acked only when the row is
 * still pending, so two pollers racing one row resolve by the write and
 * a repeated ack is a no-op. Retries carry retry_of linkage: a retry row
 * keeps thread_id on the origin row and names the origin id it retries.
 *
 * Structured receipts: every verify_request row on the wake set emits one
 * machine-readable receipt line carrying the verdict, the SHAs seen, and
 * the verification checklist.
 *
 * Watermark: the poll script keeps local state holding the last seen
 * last_edited_time and the last row id. Each tick compares fresh query
 * results against that state minus a backfill window (600 seconds), so a
 * row edited just behind the cursor is still caught. Rows already seen
 * are ignored; only unseen rows wake the agent, and the state advances
 * past them after the wake. A tick with nothing new ends silently.
 *
 * Explicit DLQ: each row tracks retry_count and last_error. After
 * MAX_ATTEMPTS failures a row is moved to invalid with an alert to the
 * alerts side chat, and is never woken again.
 *
 * Session-scoped sequencing: woken rows are grouped by thread_id and
 * delivered oldest-created-first within each thread, so one conversation
 * is always replayed in order.
 *
 * Secret scan: every inbound row is scanned for the secret-pattern
 * family (secret_, sk-, ghp_, xoxb-, ntn_). A match quarantines the row
 * at once (status to invalid plus an immediate alert) with no further
 * action; the alert names the row id and the matched pattern family
 * without copying the secret value.
 *
 * Registration: .opencode/hooks/relay/relay-hooks.json registers this
 * hook. The owner starts the loop with an explicit enable; this file
 * never enables itself and never edits the registration.
 *
 * Secrets: the Notion token, the relay-queue database id, and the
 * alerts-chat id live ONLY in the owner-held local config file (or the
 * owner shell environment) and are never hardcoded here. Missing config
 * fails closed: loud error, no query, no retry storm.
 *
 * dry_run: `node relay-poll.mjs --dry-run` runs the full pipeline against
 * simulated rows. It performs zero live reads and zero live writes; the
 * transcript states exactly what WOULD be delivered.
 */

const POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 180;
const QUIET_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 300;
// Poll target, pinned per the POLL.md consumer query (vanbu side).
const QUERY_CONSUMER = "vanbu";
const NOTION_API_BASE = "https://api.notion.com/v1";
const NOTION_VERSION = "2022-06-28";
// Quota-aware backoff ladder: 30s, then 2m, then 10m, each with jitter.
const BACKOFF_STEPS_SECONDS = [30, 120, 600];
// Degrade ladder once backoff is exhausted: 180s, then 600s, then 1800s.
const DEGRADE_CADENCES_SECONDS = [180, 600, 1800];
// Watermark backfill window: rows edited up to this far behind the cursor
// are still treated as unseen, so late edits are never skipped.
const BACKFILL_WINDOW_SECONDS = 600;
// Explicit DLQ: after this many failures a row goes to invalid plus alert.
// Knob: RELAY_MAX_ATTEMPTS in the owner environment, defaulting to 3 when absent.
const MAX_ATTEMPTS = (() => {
  const raw = process.env.RELAY_MAX_ATTEMPTS ?? null;
  const parsed = raw === null ? 3 : Number.parseInt(raw, 10);
  return Number.isFinite(parsed) && parsed > 0 ? parsed : 3;
})();
const PAGE_SIZE = 25;
// Secret-pattern family. A match quarantines the row; the alert names the
// family only and never copies the matched value.
const SECRET_PATTERNS = ["secret_", "sk-", "ghp_", "xoxb-", "ntn_"];

const args = new Set(process.argv.slice(2));
const DRY_RUN = args.has("--dry-run");
const QUIET_MODE = args.has("--quiet");

const cadenceSeconds = QUIET_MODE ? QUIET_INTERVAL_SECONDS : POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS;

function readOwnerConfig() {
  const raw = process.env.RELAY_MAX_ATTEMPTS ?? null;
  const parsed = raw === null ? 3 : Number.parseInt(raw, 10);
  return {
    token: process.env.RELAY_NOTION_TOKEN ?? null,
    databaseId: process.env.RELAY_QUEUE_DATABASE_ID ?? null,
    maxAttempts: Number.isFinite(parsed) && parsed > 0 ? parsed : 3,
  };
}

function loadWatermark() {
  if (DRY_RUN) return { lastEditedTs: "2026-10-15T07:00:00.000Z", lastRowId: "RL-1760505600-000000" };
  const file = process.env.RELAY_STATE_FILE ?? null;
  if (file === null) return { lastEditedTs: null, lastRowId: null };
  return { lastEditedTs: null, lastRowId: null, stateFile: file };
}

function makeRowId(epochSeconds, hex) {
  return `RL-${epochSeconds}-${hex}`;
}

function isQuotaError(status, bodyText) {
  if (status === 429 || status === 529) return true;
  return /rate.limit|usage.limit|quota|capacity/i.test(bodyText ?? "");
}

function retryAfterSeconds(headerValue, fallbackSeconds) {
  if (headerValue === null || headerValue === undefined) return fallbackSeconds;
  const asNumber = Number(headerValue);
  if (Number.isFinite(asNumber)) return Math.max(asNumber, 0);
  const asDate = Date.parse(headerValue);
  if (Number.isFinite(asDate)) return Math.max(Math.ceil((asDate - Date.now()) / 1000), 0);
  return fallbackSeconds;
}

function withJitter(baseSeconds) {
  return baseSeconds + Math.random() * baseSeconds * 0.25;
}

async function sleep(seconds) {
  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, seconds * 1000));
}

async function requestWithBackoff(label, doRequest) {
  let degradeIndex = 0;
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= BACKOFF_STEPS_SECONDS.length; attempt += 1) {
    const response = await doRequest();
    if (response.ok) return response;
    const bodyText = await response.text().catch(() => "");
    if (!isQuotaError(response.status, bodyText)) {
      throw new Error(`${label} failed with HTTP ${response.status}`);
    }
    if (attempt === BACKOFF_STEPS_SECONDS.length) {
      const degrade = DEGRADE_CADENCES_SECONDS[Math.min(degradeIndex, DEGRADE_CADENCES_SECONDS.length - 1)];
      throw new Error(
        `${label} quota-limited (HTTP ${response.status}); backoff 30s/2m/10m exhausted. ` +
          `DEGRADE: drop cadence toward ${degrade}s and retry next tick. No further retries this tick.`,
      );
    }
    const ladder = BACKOFF_STEPS_SECONDS[attempt];
    const wait = Math.max(
      withJitter(ladder),
      retryAfterSeconds(response.headers?.get?.("retry-after"), ladder),
    );
    console.log(`[relay-poll] quota hit (HTTP ${response.status}): backoff ${Math.round(wait)}s before retry ${attempt + 1} (Retry-After honored)`);
    await sleep(wait);
    degradeIndex += 1;
  }
  throw new Error(`${label} unreachable: backoff ladder exhausted`);
}

function simulatedRows() {
  return [
    {
      id: "RL-1760509200-a1b2c3",
      from: "opencode",
      to: "vanbu",
      type: "verify_request",
      status: "pending",
      created: "2026-10-15T08:00:00.000Z",
      lastEditedTs: "2026-10-15T08:00:00.000Z",
      threadId: "RL-1760509200-a1b2c3",
      retryCount: 0,
      lastError: null,
      evidenceShas: ["9f2c4a"],
      body: "Claim: milestone 7.7 announce is accurate. Evidence: commit 9f2c4a. Expected: catalog count matches.",
    },
    {
      id: "RL-1760509500-d4e5f6",
      from: "opencode",
      to: "vanbu",
      type: "reply",
      status: "pending",
      created: "2026-10-15T08:05:00.000Z",
      lastEditedTs: "2026-10-15T08:05:00.000Z",
      threadId: "RL-1760509200-a1b2c3",
      retryOf: "RL-1760509200-a1b2c3",
      retryCount: 0,
      lastError: null,
      body: "Answers: catalog regenerated, 41 entries. Row: RL-1760509200-a1b2c3.",
    },
    {
      id: "RL-1760509800-11aa22",
      from: "opencode",
      to: "vanbu",
      type: "announce",
      status: "pending",
      created: "2026-10-15T08:10:00.000Z",
      lastEditedTs: "2026-10-15T08:10:00.000Z",
      threadId: "RL-1760509800-11aa22",
      retryCount: 0,
      lastError: null,
      body: "Summary: hook migration landed. Hashes: 7c1e90. Gates: dry_run green.",
    },
    {
      id: "RL-1760509900-badb00",
      from: "opencode",
      to: "vanbu",
      type: "question",
      status: "pending",
      created: "2026-10-15T08:11:00.000Z",
      lastEditedTs: "2026-10-15T08:11:00.000Z",
      threadId: "RL-1760509900-badb00",
      retryCount: 0,
      lastError: null,
      body: "Question: which relay key signs receipts? Context: redacted credential material present.",
      secretFamily: "ntn_",
    },
    {
      id: "RL-1760509600-d10d10",
      from: "opencode",
      to: "vanbu",
      type: "reply",
      status: "pending",
      created: "2026-10-15T08:06:00.000Z",
      lastEditedTs: "2026-10-15T08:06:00.000Z",
      threadId: "RL-1760509600-d10d10",
      retryCount: 3,
      lastError: "claim write conflict on three consecutive ticks",
      body: "Answers: duplicate delivery attempt. Row: RL-1760509600-d10d10.",
    },
    {
      id: "RL-1760505000-9f9f9f",
      from: "opencode",
      to: "vanbu",
      type: "heartbeat",
      status: "done",
      created: "2026-10-15T06:50:00.000Z",
      lastEditedTs: "2026-10-15T06:50:00.000Z",
      threadId: "RL-1760505000-9f9f9f",
      retryCount: 0,
      lastError: null,
      body: "Sender: opencode. Uptime note: bridge alive.",
    },
    {
      id: "RL-1760505900-515151",
      from: "opencode",
      to: "vanbu",
      type: "reply",
      status: "pending",
      created: "2026-10-15T06:55:00.000Z",
      lastEditedTs: "2026-10-15T06:40:00.000Z",
      threadId: "RL-1760505900-515151",
      retryCount: 0,
      lastError: null,
      body: "Answers: stale row behind the backfill window. Row: RL-1760505900-515151.",
    },
  ];
}

function scanSecrets(row) {
  if (row.secretFamily) return row.secretFamily;
  const haystack = `${row.body ?? ""}`;
  for (const family of SECRET_PATTERNS) {
    if (haystack.includes(family)) return family;
  }
  return null;
}

function selectNewActivity(rows, watermark) {
  const floorMs =
    watermark.lastEditedTs === null
      ? null
      : Date.parse(watermark.lastEditedTs) - BACKFILL_WINDOW_SECONDS * 1000;
  return rows.filter(
    (row) =>
      row.to === QUERY_CONSUMER &&
      row.status === "pending" &&
      row.retryCount < MAX_ATTEMPTS &&
      scanSecrets(row) === null &&
      row.id !== watermark.lastRowId &&
      (floorMs === null || Date.parse(row.lastEditedTs) >= floorMs),
  );
}

function selectQuarantine(rows) {
  return rows.filter(
    (row) => row.to === QUERY_CONSUMER && row.status === "pending" && scanSecrets(row) !== null,
  );
}

function selectDeadLetter(rows) {
  return rows.filter(
    (row) =>
      row.to === QUERY_CONSUMER &&
      row.status === "pending" &&
      row.retryCount >= MAX_ATTEMPTS &&
      scanSecrets(row) === null,
  );
}

function groupByThread(rows) {
  const groups = new Map();
  for (const row of rows) {
    const key = row.threadId ?? row.id;
    if (!groups.has(key)) groups.set(key, []);
    groups.get(key).push(row);
  }
  for (const list of groups.values()) {
    list.sort((a, b) => (a.created < b.created ? -1 : a.created > b.created ? 1 : 0));
  }
  return [...groups.entries()].sort((a, b) =>
    a[1][0].created < b[1][0].created ? -1 : 1,
  );
}

function emitReceipt(row) {
  const receipt = {
    receipt_for: row.id,
    kind: "verify_receipt",
    verdict: "inconclusive",
    reason: "dry_run: envelope read only; body evidence not executed",
    shas: row.evidenceShas ?? [],
    checklist: ["schema-valid", "no-secret-hit", "evidence-present", "human-verdict-pending"],
    thread_id: row.threadId ?? row.id,
  };
  console.log(`[relay-poll] RECEIPT ${JSON.stringify(receipt)}`);
}

function readEnvelope(raw) {
  // Minimal columns on poll: only the routing envelope is projected here.
  // The page body is fetched later, and only for woken rows.
  const props = raw.properties ?? {};
  const textOf = (prop) => prop?.title?.[0]?.plain_text ?? prop?.rich_text?.[0]?.plain_text ?? null;
  const selectOf = (prop) => prop?.select?.name ?? null;
  const statusOf = (prop) => prop?.status?.name ?? null;
  return {
    pageId: raw.id ?? null,
    id: textOf(props.id),
    from: selectOf(props.from),
    to: selectOf(props.to),
    type: selectOf(props.type),
    status: statusOf(props.status),
    created: raw.created_time ?? null,
    lastEditedTs: raw.last_edited_time ?? null,
    threadId: textOf(props.thread_id),
    retryCount: props.retry_count?.number ?? 0,
    lastError: props.last_error?.rich_text?.[0]?.plain_text ?? null,
  };
}

async function queryLive(config) {
  const doRequest = () =>
    fetch(`${NOTION_API_BASE}/databases/${config.databaseId}/query`, {
      method: "POST",
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Bearer ${config.token}`,
        "Notion-Version": NOTION_VERSION,
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        filter: {
          and: [
            { property: "to", select: { equals: QUERY_CONSUMER } },
            { property: "status", status: { equals: "pending" } },
          ],
        },
        sorts: [{ property: "created", direction: "ascending" }],
        page_size: PAGE_SIZE,
      }),
    });
  const response = await requestWithBackoff("queue query", doRequest);
  const payload = await response.json();
  return (payload.results ?? []).map(readEnvelope);
}

async function fetchPageBody(config, pageId) {
  // Full fetch, wake path only: never called on a silent tick.
  const doRequest = () =>
    fetch(`${NOTION_API_BASE}/blocks/${pageId}/children?page_size=25`, {
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Bearer ${config.token}`,
        "Notion-Version": NOTION_VERSION,
      },
    });
  const response = await requestWithBackoff("page body fetch", doRequest);
  return response.json();
}

async function readRowStatus(config, pageId) {
  const doRequest = () =>
    fetch(`${NOTION_API_BASE}/pages/${pageId}`, {
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Bearer ${config.token}`,
        "Notion-Version": NOTION_VERSION,
      },
    });
  const response = await requestWithBackoff("row re-read", doRequest);
  const payload = await response.json();
  return payload.properties?.status?.status?.name ?? null;
}

async function guardedAck(config, row) {
  // Idempotent ack: write acked only when the row is still pending.
  // A repeated ack after another poller won the race is a no-op.
  const current = await readRowStatus(config, row.pageId);
  if (current !== "pending") {
    console.log(`[relay-poll] ack skipped for ${row.id}: already ${current ?? "gone"} (idempotent no-op)`);
    return false;
  }
  const doRequest = () =>
    fetch(`${NOTION_API_BASE}/pages/${row.pageId}`, {
      method: "PATCH",
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Bearer ${config.token}`,
        "Notion-Version": NOTION_VERSION,
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({ properties: { status: { status: { name: "acked" } } } }),
    });
  const response = await requestWithBackoff("claim write", doRequest);
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`claim write failed with HTTP ${response.status}`);
  return true;
}

async function markInvalid(config, row, reason) {
  const doRequest = () =>
    fetch(`${NOTION_API_BASE}/pages/${row.pageId}`, {
      method: "PATCH",
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Bearer ${config.token}`,
        "Notion-Version": NOTION_VERSION,
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({ properties: { status: { status: { name: "invalid" } } } }),
    });
  const response = await requestWithBackoff("quarantine write", doRequest);
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`quarantine write failed with HTTP ${response.status}`);
  console.log(`[relay-poll] QUARANTINE ${row.id}: invalid (${reason}); alert armed for the alerts side chat`);
}

async function main() {
  console.log(`[relay-poll] cadence=${cadenceSeconds}s quiet=${QUIET_MODE ? "on" : "off"} dry_run=${DRY_RUN ? "on" : "off"}`);
  const watermark = loadWatermark();
  console.log(`[relay-poll] watermark last_edited_time=${watermark.lastEditedTs ?? "none"} last_row_id=${watermark.lastRowId ?? "none"} backfill_window=${BACKFILL_WINDOW_SECONDS}s`);
  console.log(`[relay-poll] poll target pinned: to=${QUERY_CONSUMER} AND status=pending (server-side filter, minimal envelope; full body fetch on wake only)`);
  console.log(`[relay-poll] backoff 30s/2m/10m + jitter, Retry-After honored, 529 == 429; degrade ${DEGRADE_CADENCES_SECONDS.join("s/")}s`);

  let rows;
  if (DRY_RUN) {
    rows = simulatedRows();
    console.log(`[relay-poll] dry_run: simulated ${rows.length} rows, zero live reads, zero live writes`);
  } else {
    const config = readOwnerConfig();
    if (config.token === null || config.databaseId === null) {
      console.error("[relay-poll] REFUSED: owner Notion config absent (RELAY_NOTION_TOKEN / RELAY_QUEUE_DATABASE_ID). No query attempted.");
      process.exitCode = 1;
      return;
    }
    rows = await queryLive(config);
  }

  const quarantined = selectQuarantine(rows);
  for (const row of quarantined) {
    const family = scanSecrets(row);
    if (DRY_RUN) {
      console.log(`[relay-poll] dry_run: WOULD quarantine ${row.id} (status pending->invalid, not written); secret family=${family} (value redacted, not copied) + alert armed (not delivered)`);
    } else {
      const config = readOwnerConfig();
      await markInvalid(config, row, `secret-pattern family=${family}, value redacted`);
    }
  }

  const deadLetters = selectDeadLetter(rows);
  for (const row of deadLetters) {
    if (DRY_RUN) {
      console.log(`[relay-poll] dry_run: WOULD move ${row.id} to invalid (retry_count=${row.retryCount} >= ${MAX_ATTEMPTS}, last_error="${row.lastError}") + alert armed (not delivered, never woken)`);
    } else {
      const config = readOwnerConfig();
      await markInvalid(config, row, `dlq: retry_count=${row.retryCount} >= ${MAX_ATTEMPTS}, last_error tracked`);
    }
  }

  const fresh = selectNewActivity(rows, watermark);
  if (fresh.length === 0) {
    // COST GUARD: silent tick. No worker wakes, nothing is delivered.
    console.log("[relay-poll] no new activity: silent tick, worker stays asleep, nothing delivered");
    if (DRY_RUN) console.log("[relay-poll] RESULT: green — silent tick path exercised, cost guard holds");
    return;
  }

  const threads = groupByThread(fresh);
  const ids = fresh.map((row) => row.id).join(", ");
  if (DRY_RUN) {
    console.log(`[relay-poll] dry_run: WOULD guarded-ack ${fresh.length} row(s) [${ids}] (pending->acked only when still pending, not written; repeat ack is a no-op)`);
    console.log(`[relay-poll] dry_run: WOULD fetch full page bodies for ${fresh.length} woken row(s) only (minimal envelope on poll, not fetched)`);
    for (const [threadId, list] of threads) {
      console.log(`[relay-poll] dry_run: thread ${threadId} in order: [${list.map((r) => r.id).join(", ")}] (session-scoped sequencing)`);
    }
    for (const row of fresh) {
      if (row.type === "verify_request") emitReceipt(row);
      if (row.retryOf) {
        console.log(`[relay-poll] dry_run: retry_of linkage ${row.id} -> ${row.retryOf} via thread_id=${row.threadId} (not written)`);
      }
    }
    const newest = [...fresh].sort((a, b) => (a.lastEditedTs < b.lastEditedTs ? -1 : 1))[fresh.length - 1];
    console.log(`[relay-poll] dry_run: new id format sample ${makeRowId(1760510000, "c0ffee")} (RL-<epoch>-<hex>, unique per writer)`);
    console.log(`[relay-poll] dry_run: WOULD advance watermark to ${newest.lastEditedTs} / ${newest.id} (not written)`);
    console.log(`[relay-poll] dry_run: WOULD wake one worker with row_ids=[${ids}] for delivery to the main chat (not woken, not delivered)`);
    console.log(`[relay-poll] RESULT: green — new activity detected, single wake, main-chat delivery armed`);
    return;
  }

  const config = readOwnerConfig();
  for (const row of fresh) {
    await guardedAck(config, row);
    await fetchPageBody(config, row.pageId);
    if (row.type === "verify_request") emitReceipt(row);
  }
  console.log(`[relay-poll] WAKE worker relay-activity row_ids=[${ids}] delivery=main-chat`);
}

await main();

#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * relay-watchdog.mjs — relay queue deadline watchdog.
 *
 * Binding: DESIGN.md sections 4-5, POLL.md watchdog query, TIMEOUTS.md
 * escalation ladder, RELAY-SCHEMA.md live shape. Cadence 60 seconds. One
 * bounded REST queue query per tick for rows with status=pending AND
 * expected_reply_by in the past. Every match is delivered to the alerts
 * side chat (delivery wired in relay-hooks.json); routine traffic never
 * lands here.
 *
 * approval_request rows ALWAYS alert and are NEVER auto-approved: any
 * pending approval_request row produces an alert regardless of its
 * deadline, and this hook performs no approval action of any kind.
 *
 * REST polling: a single data-source query (POST
 * /databases/{database_id}/query) with a server-side filter
 * (status = pending AND (expected_reply_by before now OR type =
 * approval_request)), sorted by expected_reply_by ascending. There is no
 * alternate query path anywhere in this file; the network layer is plain
 * HTTPS against the Notion REST API only. Minimal columns on poll: the
 * tick reads only the routing envelope (id, from, to, type, status,
 * expected_reply_by, created, last_edited_time, thread_id,
 * announce_count); the full page body is fetched only for rows that will
 * actually alert, never on a silent tick.
 *
 * Quota-aware backoff: HTTP 429 (and 529, treated exactly as 429, plus
 * any usage-limit signal in the response body) retries on an exponential
 * ladder of 30s, then 2m, then 10m, each step with up-to-25-percent
 * jitter. A Retry-After response header is always honored and wins over
 * the ladder when it names a longer wait. When the ladder is exhausted
 * the tick degrades: the recommended cadence steps down 60s toward 600s
 * and then 1800s and the failure is logged loudly instead of retried
 * further, so a quota event can never become a retry storm.
 *
 * Idempotency: alert tasks carry ids of the form
 * relay-alert-<epoch>-<hex> (epoch seconds plus random lowercase hex),
 * unique per alert without coordination. Alerting is ledger-guarded: the
 * sweep ledger maps each row id to its announce count, so one sweep
 * emits at most one alert per row and a repeated sweep never duplicates
 * an alert for the same announcement round. Marking a row invalid is a
 * guarded transition written only when the row is still pending.
 *
 * Structured receipts: every verify_request row that alerts emits one
 * machine-readable receipt line carrying the verdict, the SHAs seen, and
 * the verification checklist.
 *
 * Watermark: the watchdog keeps local state holding the last sweep
 * timestamp (last_edited_time cursor) plus the per-row announce ledger.
 * Each tick sweeps rows against that cursor minus a backfill window (600
 * seconds), so a row edited just behind the cursor is still caught. The
 * cursor advances after every sweep; a tick with nothing overdue ends
 * silently.
 *
 * Explicit DLQ: each row tracks retry_count (here: announce_count) and
 * last_error. After MAX_ATTEMPTS unanswered announcements a row is moved
 * to invalid with an escalated alert naming the stall, per the TIMEOUTS.md
 * repeated-stall rung, and is never alerted again.
 *
 * Session-scoped sequencing: alerts are grouped by thread_id and ordered
 * oldest-deadline-first within each thread, so one conversation escalates
 * in order.
 *
 * Secret scan: every swept row is scanned for the secret-pattern family
 * (secret_, sk-, ghp_, xoxb-, ntn_). A match quarantines the row at once
 * (status to invalid plus an immediate alert) with no further action; the
 * alert names the row id and the matched pattern family without copying
 * the secret value.
 *
 * Registration: .opencode/hooks/relay/relay-hooks.json registers this
 * hook DISABLED. The owner starts the loop with an explicit enable; this
 * file never enables itself and never edits the registration.
 *
 * Secrets: the Notion token, the relay-queue database id, and the
 * alerts-chat id live ONLY in the owner-held local config file (or the
 * owner shell environment) and are never hardcoded here. Missing config
 * fails closed: loud error, no query, no retry storm.
 *
 * dry_run: `node relay-watchdog.mjs --dry-run` runs the full pipeline
 * against simulated rows. It performs zero live reads and zero live
 * writes; the transcript states exactly what WOULD be delivered.
 */

const WATCHDOG_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 60;
const NOTION_API_BASE = "https://api.notion.com/v1";
const NOTION_VERSION = "2022-06-28";
// Quota-aware backoff ladder: 30s, then 2m, then 10m, each with jitter.
const BACKOFF_STEPS_SECONDS = [30, 120, 600];
// Degrade ladder once backoff is exhausted: 60s, then 600s, then 1800s.
const DEGRADE_CADENCES_SECONDS = [60, 600, 1800];
// Watermark backfill window: rows edited up to this far behind the sweep
// cursor are still swept, so late edits are never skipped.
const BACKFILL_WINDOW_SECONDS = 600;
// Explicit DLQ: after this many unanswered announcements a row goes to
// invalid with an escalated alert and is never alerted again.
// Knob: RELAY_MAX_ATTEMPTS in the owner environment, defaulting to 3 when absent.
const MAX_ATTEMPTS = (() => {
  const raw = process.env.RELAY_MAX_ATTEMPTS ?? null;
  const parsed = raw === null ? 3 : Number.parseInt(raw, 10);
  return Number.isFinite(parsed) && parsed > 0 ? parsed : 3;
})();
const PAGE_SIZE = 25;
// Secret-pattern family. A match quarantines the row; the alert names the
// family only and never copies the matched value.
const SECRET_PATTERNS = ["secret_", "sk-", "ghp_", "xoxb-", "ntn_"];

const args = new Set(process.argv.slice(2));
const DRY_RUN = args.has("--dry-run");

function readOwnerConfig() {
  const raw = process.env.RELAY_MAX_ATTEMPTS ?? null;
  const parsed = raw === null ? 3 : Number.parseInt(raw, 10);
  return {
    token: process.env.RELAY_NOTION_TOKEN ?? null,
    databaseId: process.env.RELAY_QUEUE_DATABASE_ID ?? null,
    alertsChat: process.env.RELAY_ALERTS_CHAT_ID ?? null,
    maxAttempts: Number.isFinite(parsed) && parsed > 0 ? parsed : 3,
  };
}

function loadSweepState() {
  if (DRY_RUN) {
    return {
      lastSweepTs: "2026-10-15T07:00:00.000Z",
      ledger: {},
    };
  }
  const file = process.env.RELAY_WATCHDOG_STATE_FILE ?? null;
  if (file === null) return { lastSweepTs: null, ledger: {} };
  return { lastSweepTs: null, ledger: {}, stateFile: file };
}

function makeAlertId(epochSeconds, hex) {
  return `relay-alert-${epochSeconds}-${hex}`;
}

function isQuotaError(status, bodyText) {
  if (status === 429 || status === 529) return true;
  return /rate.limit|usage.limit|quota|capacity/i.test(bodyText ?? "");
}

function retryAfterSeconds(headerValue, fallbackSeconds) {
  if (headerValue === null || headerValue === undefined) return fallbackSeconds;
  const asNumber = Number(headerValue);
  if (Number.isFinite(asNumber)) return Math.max(asNumber, 0);
  const asDate = Date.parse(headerValue);
  if (Number.isFinite(asDate)) return Math.max(Math.ceil((asDate - Date.now()) / 1000), 0);
  return fallbackSeconds;
}

function withJitter(baseSeconds) {
  return baseSeconds + Math.random() * baseSeconds * 0.25;
}

async function sleep(seconds) {
  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, seconds * 1000));
}

async function requestWithBackoff(label, doRequest) {
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= BACKOFF_STEPS_SECONDS.length; attempt += 1) {
    const response = await doRequest();
    if (response.ok) return response;
    const bodyText = await response.text().catch(() => "");
    if (!isQuotaError(response.status, bodyText)) {
      throw new Error(`${label} failed with HTTP ${response.status}`);
    }
    if (attempt === BACKOFF_STEPS_SECONDS.length) {
      const degrade = DEGRADE_CADENCES_SECONDS[DEGRADE_CADENCES_SECONDS.length - 1];
      throw new Error(
        `${label} quota-limited (HTTP ${response.status}); backoff 30s/2m/10m exhausted. ` +
          `DEGRADE: drop cadence toward ${degrade}s and retry next tick. No further retries this tick.`,
      );
    }
    const ladder = BACKOFF_STEPS_SECONDS[attempt];
    const wait = Math.max(
      withJitter(ladder),
      retryAfterSeconds(response.headers?.get?.("retry-after"), ladder),
    );
    console.log(`[relay-watchdog] quota hit (HTTP ${response.status}): backoff ${Math.round(wait)}s before retry ${attempt + 1} (Retry-After honored)`);
    await sleep(wait);
  }
  throw new Error(`${label} unreachable: backoff ladder exhausted`);
}

function simulatedRows(nowMs) {
  return [
    {
      pageId: null,
      id: "RL-1760502000-2b2b2b",
      from: "vanbu",
      to: "opencode",
      type: "verify_request",
      status: "pending",
      announceCount: 1,
      lastError: "no reply within estimate",
      // Long past: always overdue, deterministic in dry_run.
      expectedReplyBy: "2000-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
      created: "1999-12-31T23:00:00.000Z",
      lastEditedTs: "1999-12-31T23:30:00.000Z",
      threadId: "RL-1760502000-2b2b2b",
      evidenceShas: ["4d5e6f"],
      body: "Claim: watchdog receipt path works. Evidence: commit 4d5e6f. Expected: one receipt per verify_request.",
    },
    {
      pageId: null,
      id: "RL-1760511000-3c3c3c",
      from: "vanbu",
      to: "omar",
      type: "approval_request",
      status: "pending",
      announceCount: 0,
      lastError: null,
      // Far future: NOT overdue, yet must still alert (approval rule).
      expectedReplyBy: "2100-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
      created: "2026-10-15T08:30:00.000Z",
      lastEditedTs: "2026-10-15T08:30:00.000Z",
      threadId: "RL-1760511000-3c3c3c",
      body: "Proposal: publish the 7.7 notes. Risk: premature announcement. Needed by: 2100-01-01.",
    },
    {
      pageId: null,
      id: "RL-1760512000-4d4d4d",
      from: "opencode",
      to: "vanbu",
      type: "reply",
      status: "pending",
      announceCount: 0,
      lastError: null,
      // Far future: not overdue, routine, stays silent.
      expectedReplyBy: "2100-01-01T01:00:00.000Z",
      created: "2026-10-15T08:40:00.000Z",
      lastEditedTs: "2026-10-15T08:40:00.000Z",
      threadId: "RL-1760512000-4d4d4d",
      body: "Answers: routine progress note. Row: RL-1760512000-4d4d4d.",
    },
    {
      pageId: null,
      id: "RL-1760501000-5e5e5e",
      from: "vanbu",
      to: "opencode",
      type: "reply",
      status: "done",
      announceCount: 1,
      lastError: null,
      expectedReplyBy: "2000-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
      created: "1999-12-31T22:00:00.000Z",
      lastEditedTs: "1999-12-31T22:30:00.000Z",
      threadId: "RL-1760501000-5e5e5e",
      body: "Answers: already closed. Row: RL-1760501000-5e5e5e.",
    },
    {
      pageId: null,
      id: "RL-1760513000-6f6f6f",
      from: "vanbu",
      to: "opencode",
      type: "question",
      status: "pending",
      announceCount: 0,
      lastError: null,
      expectedReplyBy: "2000-01-01T02:00:00.000Z",
      created: "2026-10-15T08:45:00.000Z",
      lastEditedTs: "2026-10-15T08:45:00.000Z",
      threadId: "RL-1760513000-6f6f6f",
      body: "Question: which credential signs the sweep? Context: redacted material present.",
      secretFamily: "ntn_",
    },
    {
      pageId: null,
      id: "RL-1760500000-7a7a7a",
      from: "vanbu",
      to: "opencode",
      type: "verify_request",
      status: "pending",
      announceCount: 3,
      lastError: "three sweeps with no reply and no progress",
      expectedReplyBy: "2000-01-01T03:00:00.000Z",
      created: "1999-12-31T20:00:00.000Z",
      lastEditedTs: "1999-12-31T21:00:00.000Z",
      threadId: "RL-1760500000-7a7a7a",
      evidenceShas: [],
      body: "Claim: stalled verification. Evidence: none new. Expected: owner nudge.",
    },
  ].map((row) => ({ ...row, overdue: row.status === "pending" && Date.parse(row.expectedReplyBy) < nowMs }));
}

function scanSecrets(row) {
  if (row.secretFamily) return row.secretFamily;
  const haystack = `${row.body ?? ""}`;
  for (const family of SECRET_PATTERNS) {
    if (haystack.includes(family)) return family;
  }
  return null;
}

function selectAlerts(rows) {
  const overdue = rows.filter((row) => row.status === "pending" && row.overdue && scanSecrets(row) === null && (row.announceCount ?? 0) < MAX_ATTEMPTS);
  const approvals = rows.filter((row) => row.status === "pending" && row.type === "approval_request" && scanSecrets(row) === null);
  const seen = new Set();
  return [...overdue, ...approvals].filter((row) => {
    if (seen.has(row.id)) return false;
    seen.add(row.id);
    return true;
  });
}

function selectQuarantine(rows) {
  return rows.filter((row) => row.status === "pending" && scanSecrets(row) !== null);
}

function selectDeadLetter(rows) {
  return rows.filter(
    (row) =>
      row.status === "pending" &&
      row.overdue &&
      (row.announceCount ?? 0) >= MAX_ATTEMPTS &&
      scanSecrets(row) === null,
  );
}

function groupByThread(rows) {
  const groups = new Map();
  for (const row of rows) {
    const key = row.threadId ?? row.id;
    if (!groups.has(key)) groups.set(key, []);
    groups.get(key).push(row);
  }
  for (const list of groups.values()) {
    list.sort((a, b) => (a.expectedReplyBy < b.expectedReplyBy ? -1 : a.expectedReplyBy > b.expectedReplyBy ? 1 : 0));
  }
  return [...groups.entries()].sort((a, b) =>
    a[1][0].expectedReplyBy < b[1][0].expectedReplyBy ? -1 : 1,
  );
}

function emitReceipt(row, verdict, reason) {
  const receipt = {
    receipt_for: row.id,
    kind: "verify_receipt",
    verdict,
    reason,
    shas: row.evidenceShas ?? [],
    checklist: ["schema-valid", "no-secret-hit", "deadline-checked", "human-verdict-pending"],
    thread_id: row.threadId ?? row.id,
  };
  console.log(`[relay-watchdog] RECEIPT ${JSON.stringify(receipt)}`);
}

function readEnvelope(raw) {
  // Minimal columns on poll: only the routing envelope is projected here.
  // The page body is fetched later, and only for rows that will alert.
  const props = raw.properties ?? {};
  const textOf = (prop) => prop?.title?.[0]?.plain_text ?? prop?.rich_text?.[0]?.plain_text ?? null;
  const selectOf = (prop) => prop?.select?.name ?? null;
  const statusOf = (prop) => prop?.status?.name ?? null;
  const dateOf = (prop) => prop?.date?.start ?? null;
  return {
    pageId: raw.id ?? null,
    id: textOf(props.id),
    from: selectOf(props.from),
    to: selectOf(props.to),
    type: selectOf(props.type),
    status: statusOf(props.status),
    expectedReplyBy: dateOf(props.expected_reply_by),
    created: raw.created_time ?? null,
    lastEditedTs: raw.last_edited_time ?? null,
    threadId: textOf(props.thread_id),
    announceCount: props.announce_count?.number ?? 0,
    lastError: props.last_error?.rich_text?.[0]?.plain_text ?? null,
  };
}

async function queryLive(config) {
  const doRequest = () =>
    fetch(`${NOTION_API_BASE}/databases/${config.databaseId}/query`, {
      method: "POST",
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Bearer ${config.token}`,
        "Notion-Version": NOTION_VERSION,
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        filter: {
          and: [
            { property: "status", status: { equals: "pending" } },
            {
              or: [
                { property: "expected_reply_by", date: { before: new Date().toISOString() } },
                { property: "type", select: { equals: "approval_request" } },
              ],
            },
          ],
        },
        sorts: [{ property: "expected_reply_by", direction: "ascending" }],
        page_size: PAGE_SIZE,
      }),
    });
  const response = await requestWithBackoff("watchdog query", doRequest);
  const payload = await response.json();
  const nowMs = Date.now();
  return (payload.results ?? [])
    .map(readEnvelope)
    .map((row) => ({
      ...row,
      overdue: row.status === "pending" && row.expectedReplyBy !== null && Date.parse(row.expectedReplyBy) < nowMs,
    }));
}

async function readRowStatus(config, pageId) {
  const doRequest = () =>
    fetch(`${NOTION_API_BASE}/pages/${pageId}`, {
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Bearer ${config.token}`,
        "Notion-Version": NOTION_VERSION,
      },
    });
  const response = await requestWithBackoff("row re-read", doRequest);
  const payload = await response.json();
  return payload.properties?.status?.status?.name ?? null;
}

async function markInvalid(config, row, reason) {
  // Guarded transition: write invalid only when the row is still pending.
  const current = await readRowStatus(config, row.pageId);
  if (current !== "pending") {
    console.log(`[relay-watchdog] quarantine skipped for ${row.id}: already ${current ?? "gone"} (idempotent no-op)`);
    return;
  }
  const doRequest = () =>
    fetch(`${NOTION_API_BASE}/pages/${row.pageId}`, {
      method: "PATCH",
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Bearer ${config.token}`,
        "Notion-Version": NOTION_VERSION,
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({ properties: { status: { status: { name: "invalid" } } } }),
    });
  const response = await requestWithBackoff("quarantine write", doRequest);
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`quarantine write failed with HTTP ${response.status}`);
  console.log(`[relay-watchdog] QUARANTINE ${row.id}: invalid (${reason}); alert armed for the alerts side chat`);
}

async function main() {
  const nowMs = Date.now();
  const nowIso = new Date(nowMs).toISOString();
  console.log(`[relay-watchdog] cadence=${WATCHDOG_INTERVAL_SECONDS}s dry_run=${DRY_RUN ? "on" : "off"}`);
  const sweep = loadSweepState();
  console.log(`[relay-watchdog] sweep cursor last_edited_time=${sweep.lastSweepTs ?? "none"} backfill_window=${BACKFILL_WINDOW_SECONDS}s ledger_rows=${Object.keys(sweep.ledger).length}`);
  console.log(`[relay-watchdog] watchdog filter pinned: status=pending AND (expected_reply_by < now OR type=approval_request), server-side, minimal envelope; full body fetch on alert only`);
  console.log(`[relay-watchdog] backoff 30s/2m/10m + jitter, Retry-After honored, 529 == 429; degrade ${DEGRADE_CADENCES_SECONDS.join("s/")}s`);

  let rows;
  let alertsTarget;
  if (DRY_RUN) {
    rows = simulatedRows(nowMs);
    alertsTarget = "<alerts-side-chat; owner config, not hardcoded>";
    console.log(`[relay-watchdog] dry_run: simulated ${rows.length} rows, zero live reads, zero live writes`);
  } else {
    const config = readOwnerConfig();
    if (config.token === null || config.databaseId === null || config.alertsChat === null) {
      console.error("[relay-watchdog] REFUSED: owner config absent (RELAY_NOTION_TOKEN / RELAY_QUEUE_DATABASE_ID / RELAY_ALERTS_CHAT_ID). No query attempted.");
      process.exitCode = 1;
      return;
    }
    rows = await queryLive(config);
    alertsTarget = "alerts side chat (owner-configured id)";
  }

  const quarantined = selectQuarantine(rows);
  for (const row of quarantined) {
    const family = scanSecrets(row);
    if (DRY_RUN) {
      console.log(`[relay-watchdog] dry_run: WOULD quarantine ${row.id} (status pending->invalid, not written); secret family=${family} (value redacted, not copied) + alert armed (not delivered)`);
    } else {
      const config = readOwnerConfig();
      await markInvalid(config, row, `secret-pattern family=${family}, value redacted`);
    }
  }

  const deadLetters = selectDeadLetter(rows);
  for (const row of deadLetters) {
    if (DRY_RUN) {
      console.log(`[relay-watchdog] dry_run: WOULD move ${row.id} to invalid (announce_count=${row.announceCount} >= ${MAX_ATTEMPTS}, last_error="${row.lastError}") + escalated stall alert armed for ${alertsTarget} (not delivered, never alerted again)`);
      emitReceipt(row, "unanswered", "dry_run: three sweeps with no reply and no progress; escalated per repeated-stall rung");
    } else {
      const config = readOwnerConfig();
      await markInvalid(config, row, `dlq: announce_count=${row.announceCount} >= ${MAX_ATTEMPTS}, last_error tracked`);
    }
  }

  const alerts = selectAlerts(rows);
  if (alerts.length === 0 && quarantined.length === 0 && deadLetters.length === 0) {
    console.log("[relay-watchdog] no overdue or approval rows: silent tick, nothing delivered");
    if (DRY_RUN) console.log("[relay-watchdog] RESULT: green — silent tick path exercised");
    return;
  }

  const threads = groupByThread(alerts);
  for (const [threadId, list] of threads) {
    if (DRY_RUN) {
      console.log(`[relay-watchdog] dry_run: thread ${threadId} in order: [${list.map((r) => r.id).join(", ")}] (session-scoped sequencing)`);
    }
    for (const row of list) {
      const reason = row.type === "approval_request" ? "approval_request-always-alerts" : "deadline-passed";
      const alertId = DRY_RUN ? makeAlertId(1760510000, "a1b2c3") : makeAlertId(Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000), Math.random().toString(16).slice(2, 8));
      if (DRY_RUN) {
        console.log(`[relay-watchdog] dry_run: WOULD deliver alert ${alertId} for ${row.id} (type=${row.type} reason=${reason}) to ${alertsTarget} (not delivered; ledger-guarded, one alert per row per sweep)`);
        if (row.type === "verify_request") {
          emitReceipt(row, "unanswered", "dry_run: still pending past expected_reply_by; body evidence not executed");
        }
      } else {
        console.log(`[relay-watchdog] ALERT ${alertId} ${row.id} (type=${row.type} reason=${reason}) delivery=alerts-side-chat`);
        if (row.type === "verify_request") {
          emitReceipt(row, "unanswered", "still pending past expected_reply_by");
        }
      }
    }
  }
  if (DRY_RUN) {
    console.log(`[relay-watchdog] dry_run: sweep cursor WOULD advance to ${nowIso} (not written)`);
    console.log(`[relay-watchdog] dry_run: zero approvals performed — approval_request rows alert, never auto-approved (not written)`);
    console.log(`[relay-watchdog] RESULT: green — ${alerts.length} alert(s) armed for the alerts side chat`);
  }
}

await main();

<!-- BEGIN VERBATIM: .githooks/commit-msg -->
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# commit-msg — zero AI attribution gate for commit messages.
#
# Companion to .githooks/pre-commit: that hook scans staged content, this one
# scans the message itself. Rejects trailers and footers such as
# "Co-authored-by: Claude" or "Generated with Claude Code".
#
# Activate with:  bash scripts/setup-git-hooks.sh

set -u

# Built from byte escapes so this hook's own source never contains the literal,
# which pre-commit's scan of staged content would otherwise match.
ROBOT_EMOJI="$(printf '\xF0\x9F\xA4\x96')"

if [ "$#" -lt 1 ] || [ -z "${1:-}" ]; then
    printf 'COMMIT-MSG REJECTED: no message file was passed to the hook.\n' >&2
    exit 1
fi

MSG_FILE="$1"

if [ ! -f "$MSG_FILE" ]; then
    printf 'COMMIT-MSG REJECTED: message file %s not found.\n' "$MSG_FILE" >&2
    exit 1
fi

if grep -iqE "co-authored-by:.*(claude|anthropic)|generated (with|by|using).*(claude|anthropic)|${ROBOT_EMOJI}" "$MSG_FILE"; then
    cat >&2 <<'EOF'
COMMIT-MSG REJECTED: the commit message contains AI attribution.
This repository enforces zero AI attribution in its history.
EOF
    exit 1
fi

exit 0

<!-- END VERBATIM: .githooks/commit-msg -->

<!-- BEGIN VERBATIM: .githooks/pre-commit -->
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# pre-commit — secret scanner and zero-attribution gate.
#
# Activate with:  bash scripts/setup-git-hooks.sh   (git config core.hooksPath .githooks)
#
# Rejects the commit when staged content contains:
#   1. API keys and credential-shaped literals in added lines — Anthropic,
#      OpenRouter, GitHub, and Slack token prefixes, an AWS access-key id, a
#      bearer token inside an Authorization header, and a generic
#      KEY/SECRET/TOKEN/PASSWORD assignment to a long literal.
#   2. a new file named .env, because .env.example carries stand-ins only.
#   3. AI attribution markers, such as a Claude co-author trailer.
#
# Substitution shapes are let through: ${VAR}, <VALUE>, your-*, changeme,
# example, and xxxx, because that is exactly how .env.example must look.
#
# Targeted key patterns and an assignment heuristic rather than full entropy
# math: swap in gitleaks if scanning ever needs to grow beyond this.

set -u

VIOLATIONS=0

# Built from byte escapes so this hook's own source never contains the literal,
# which the staged-content scan below would otherwise match against itself.
ROBOT_EMOJI="$(printf '\xF0\x9F\xA4\x96')"

fail() {
    printf 'PRE-COMMIT REJECTED: %s\n' "$*" >&2
    VIOLATIONS=$((VIOLATIONS + 1))
}

# Added lines of staged changes (A/C/M/R), without the +++ file header.
ADDED_LINES="$(git diff --cached --unified=0 --diff-filter=ACMR -- 2> /dev/null | grep -E '^\+' | grep -vE '^\+\+\+')"

if [ -n "$ADDED_LINES" ]; then
    # 1a. Known API key formats.
    if printf '%s\n' "$ADDED_LINES" | grep -EqE \
        'sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}|sk-or-v1-[A-Za-z0-9]{16,}|gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{36,}|github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{22,}|xox[abprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,}|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}'; then
        fail 'staged diff contains a known API key format (sk-ant-*, sk-or-v1-*, gh*_*, github_pat_*, xox*-*, AKIA*).'
    fi

    # 1b. Credential-shaped assignments, per line.
    SUSPECT_ASSIGN="$(printf '%s\n' "$ADDED_LINES" \
        | grep -iE "(api[_-]?key|secret|token|password)[\"']?[[:space:]]*[:=][[:space:]]*[\"']?[A-Za-z0-9+/_=-]{24,}" \
        | grep -ivE 'your[_-]|changeme|example|\$\{|<[^>]+>|xxxx' || true)"
    if [ -n "$SUSPECT_ASSIGN" ]; then
        fail 'staged diff contains a credential-shaped assignment (KEY/SECRET/TOKEN/PASSWORD set to a long literal).'
    fi

    # 1c. Bearer token inside a JSON or YAML Authorization header. Written so
    #     this hook's own source never matches it.
    if printf '%s\n' "$ADDED_LINES" | grep -EqiE \
        '"authorization"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"bearer [A-Za-z0-9+/_=-]{24,}"'; then
        fail 'staged diff contains a bearer token in an Authorization header; reference credentials by environment variable name only.'
    fi

    # 2. AI attribution inside staged content. Textual markers match only as
    #    trailer-shaped lines at line start, so documentation ABOUT the rule —
    #    including this hook's own source — is not itself rejected. The badge
    #    emoji stays unanchored.
    if printf '%s\n' "$ADDED_LINES" | grep -iqE \
        "^\+[[:space:]]*(co-authored-by:.*(claude|anthropic)|generated (with|by|using)[[:space:]].*(claude|anthropic))|${ROBOT_EMOJI}"; then
        fail 'staged diff contains AI attribution markers; this repository ships zero AI attribution.'
    fi
fi

# 3. A literal .env file must never be committed; .env.example is fine.
if git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=A 2> /dev/null | grep -Eq '(^|/)\.env$'; then
    fail 'staged changes add a .env file; real values live outside version control.'
fi

if [ "$VIOLATIONS" -gt 0 ]; then
    printf '\n%d violation(s). Fix the staged content and try again.\n' "$VIOLATIONS" >&2
    exit 1
fi

exit 0

<!-- END VERBATIM: .githooks/pre-commit -->

tsconfig.json | 25 | 1200 | sha256=98758892668a49623545b663744f89112de92fdd2b201cd6322b2daa50d999d4
<!-- BEGIN VERBATIM: tsconfig.json -->
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    // Node 25 is the declared runtime; es2022 is a conservative floor that
    // covers every construct the plugin uses (??, ?., numeric separators,
    // Array.prototype.flatMap, Set/Map, satisfies).
    "target": "es2022",
    // Named rather than the default es2022.full, so no DOM global is ambient.
    // A Node-only plugin that reaches for `document` or `fetch` should fail.
    "lib": ["es2022"],
    // The plugin is an ES module: it exports a default and uses dynamic import()
    // for the Node built-ins. nodenext matches how Node 25 actually loads it.
    "module": "nodenext",
    "moduleResolution": "nodenext",
    "strict": true,
    // The gate is a check, not a build: nothing is emitted.
    "noEmit": true,
    // This repository is dependency-free by design, so no ambient @types package
    // is assumed. Keeps the result identical on a clean CI checkout and in a
    // developer tree that happens to have unrelated packages installed.
    "types": []
  },
  // Named explicitly rather than globbed. A glob would pull in registry JSONL
  // sidecars, scripts, and stray files that are not TypeScript.
  "files": [".opencode/plugin/arsenal.ts"]
}

<!-- END VERBATIM: tsconfig.json -->

## 10. Documentation links

Verdict: FAIL — 11 HIGH stale-census and invented-identifier defects, 14 MEDIUM, 4 LOW. The
first-party Markdown resolves cleanly; the archive file, the generated surfaces, and the SVG alt texts
do not.

### 10.1 Link sweep, re-run live

Method (`§14` R-7): match `/\]\(([^)#\s]+)(#[^)\s]*)?\)/g` per file, skip absolute, `mailto:`, and
anchor targets, resolve each relative target against the file's own directory. The repository ships no
link-checker script; the sweep is purpose-built and its totals are regex-sensitive (`§1.6`).

| Scope | Files | Link tokens | Broken | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| first-party (docs minus `docs/99-archive`, `.opencode` Markdown, root `*.md`) | 175 | 307 | 0 real | two further tokens at `.opencode/audit/V87-FEATURE-AUDIT-2.md:279`, `:285` are `htt…` text quoted inside backticks — matched by a naive sweep, not links |
| archive (`docs/99-archive/`) | 44 | 10 | 10 | all ten in one file (`§12` L13-10-045) |
| registry generated surfaces | 12 files | 32 truncated `](`-tokens | n/a | disposition in `§10.5` |

Instrument delta, stated plainly: the dispatch recorded 176 files and 308 tokens for the same
first-party scope; this pass measured 175 and 307 with the regex above. The one-file, one-token delta
is exactly what a heuristic total cannot resolve, and no broken-target verdict changes either way.

The ten archive breakages are all in `docs/99-archive/VTA-FACTORY-PLAN-SURGICAL.md`, at lines `:34`,
`:35` (two tokens), `:36`, `:88`, `:134`, `:180`, `:227`, `:269`, `:305`; each token is a
repository-root-relative path (`AGENTS.md`, `WORKFLOW.md`, `kit/kit.lock`, `registry/catalog.json`,
`SECURITY.md`) that resolved while the file sat at the repository root and stopped resolving when the
file moved under `docs/99-archive/`. Verbatim, `.opencode/commands/V-FULL-AUDIT.md` itself is not
affected; the file's own lines read
`docs/99-archive/VTA-FACTORY-PLAN-SURGICAL.md:34: `registry/catalog.json`. Standalone governance:
[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md),` and `:35: [WORKFLOW.md](WORKFLOW.md), [kit/kit.lock](kit/kit.lock),`. The
classification was settled previously: `git log --oneline` shows the file arrived with commit `c7c762c`,
so these are live first-party links, not frozen history (`§14` R-9 `git log --oneline -3`).

## 12. Ranked findings

Ranking is worst-first across all areas. **67 findings: 19 HIGH, 31 MEDIUM,
17 LOW.** Each finding carries exactly one Law-13 identifier of the form `L13-<SS>-<NNN>`, where
`<SS>` is the REPORT-SPEC section the finding belongs to and `<NNN>` is the global worst-first rank
(001 = worst). Identifier order therefore matches rank order, and the identifier set is in one-to-one
correspondence with the defect set (`§14` G-3). Every finding quotes the exact source line(s) it rests
on; the fullest quote for each lives in the section it belongs to (`§3`…`§11`).

Ranking principle, stated so the order can be audited: guard defects that can modify files or corrupt
verdicts first; then provisioning targets that resolve to nothing (the lock, the commands, the theme
registry); then dispatch-mechanism claims; then misleading census claims in reader-facing documents
(entry points before mirrors before dev pages); then gate-coverage and provenance gaps; then wording,
hygiene, and recorded-by-design items.

### 12.1 HIGH — 19 findings

**L13-09-001 — the two after-guards fire on reads of JavaScript and TypeScript paths.** Locations:
`.opencode/plugin/arsenal.ts:1731-1734` and `.opencode/plugin/arsenal.ts:1796-1799`; destructive argv at
`.opencode/plugin/arsenal.ts:1821-1826`. Both guards select by extension alone and never consult the
tool name, though `.opencode/plugin/arsenal.ts:491` defines `WRITE_TOOLS` and `:1685` applies it
elsewhere. `[…prettier.prefixArgs, "--write", "--ignore-unknown", "--log-level", "warn", ...paths]`
(`:1824`) means a read can rewrite files. Ranked first: the only finding that can modify files without
a write. Detail in `§9.1`.

**L13-09-002 — the toolchain resolver returns the host binary, so the typecheck fails falsely and
pollutes the circuit ledger.** Location: `.opencode/plugin/arsenal.ts:895-896`; consequence at `:1779`
and `:1782`. `command: rt.proc.execPath.length > 0 ? rt.proc.execPath : "node"` resolves to the host
CLI, which then parses `--noEmit` and rejects it; `state.circuit.failures += 1` records the fake
failure. Detail in `§9.2`.

**L13-03-003 — two pending kit themes target agent ids that no longer exist, and the gate is hard-coded
around the same dead ids.** Locations: `kit/kit.lock:167`
(`"id": "vantrilex-ai-generated-code-security-auditor"`) and `kit/kit.lock:170`
(`"id": "vantrilex-technical-writer"`); the live files are `vantrilex-security-auditor` and
`vantrilex-scribe` (`§2.4`). `scripts/verify-kit.mjs:33` and `:36` carry the same two dead strings in
`EXPECTED_PENDING`, and `:1399` fails a *corrected* id as "unexpected pending entry". Detail in `§3.2`.

### 12.5 The two merges applied to new findings, and why

The dispatch's merge rule is explicit: same file plus same defect duplicates merge; per-surface siblings
stay separate. Two of the twenty-two new findings are the same defect in the same file as a carried row,
so each was folded into that row and its new site is cited there:

| New finding | Merged into | Reason | New site now cited |
|---|---|---|---|
| `N12` (`README.md:44` "ten agent files") | L13-10-009 | same file, same defect as `README.md:167`/`:331-333` (the agent-count and roster claim) | `README.md:44` |
| `N13` (`README.md:228` 2,804 records / 8 kinds, `:232` "live verified counts") | L13-10-012 | same file, same defect as `README.md:164-170` (the catalog census and its liveness claim) | `README.md:228`, `:232` |

This is why the ranked set holds 67 rows rather than 69 = 47 + 22. The two merges are
reversible in one line each: splitting `README.md:44` out of L13-10-009 and `README.md:228`/`:232` out of
L13-10-012 would yield 69 rows without changing any evidence.

Fix sequencing (earlier waves unblock later ones; the shared root cause is named once):

**Shared root cause — the bare-stem to `vantrilex-*` agent rename was never reconciled across every
surface.** The rename replaced seven bare-stem agent files with seven `vantrilex-*` files
(`§14` R-9 git status: `D .opencode/agents/agent-maker.md`, `ai-generated-code-security-auditor.md`,
`architect.md`, `code-reviewer.md`, `kit-maintainer.md`, `red-team.md`, `technical-writer.md`; `??`
`vantrilex-agent-maker.md`, `vantrilex-architect.md`, `vantrilex-code-reviewer.md`,
`vantrilex-kit-maintainer.md`, `vantrilex-puller.md`, `vantrilex-red-team.md`,
`vantrilex-uploader.md`). The surfaces that still carry the old names are: the lock's pending list
(L13-03-003), the atomic-switch theme registry (L13-04-007), the doubled-prefix pending ids and the
three V-switch commands (L13-03-020), two consult commands (L13-08-004, L13-08-005), the README roster
(L13-10-009), the AI-guide table (L13-10-010), the Arabic roster (L13-10-011), the Arabic lock page
(L13-10-017), the singular role path (L13-10-046), and the index itself (L13-07-036). Landing them in
one wave closes the family in one review rather than in ten partial ones.

| Wave | Findings | Why this order |
|---|---|---|
| W-A | L13-09-001, L13-09-002 | the guard defects can corrupt files and verdicts while other fixes are landing; repair them first |
| W-B | L13-03-003, L13-03-020, L13-03-021, L13-03-022, L13-03-051 | one owner holds the lock; the id repairs must land with the verifier change or the gate stays blind |
| W-C | L13-04-007, L13-08-004, L13-08-005, L13-06-026, L13-07-036 | the rename-reconciliation remainder: registry map, two consult commands, lock/catalog rows, and the git index |
| W-D | L13-05-006, L13-05-023, L13-05-024, L13-04-025, L13-04-053, L13-05-052 | one regeneration cycle closes the data-plane findings; the changelog line belongs with the same change |
| W-E | L13-10-009…L13-10-019, L13-10-037…L13-10-050, L13-10-063…L13-10-066, L13-06-058 | every census rewrite draws from one recounted source (`§2`), so they land together and cannot cross-stale |
| W-F | L13-07-029, L13-08-030, L13-08-031, L13-09-032…L13-09-035, L13-09-061, L13-09-062, L13-09-067, L13-07-054…L13-07-057, L13-08-059, L13-08-060, L13-06-027, L13-06-028 | component-level edits with local proofs; the two agent-doctrine items (027, 028) need the owner ruling and the V2 probe, so they close last of this wave |
